See [Setting up a Basemap and Overlaying Points from PostGIS](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-basemap-postgis/index.md>) for a discussion of why a tiling step is needed and what OpenMapTiles is, and [the tile source comparison](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-tiles/index.md>) for the pros and cons of the different archive formats.

```bash
mkdir --parents data
docker run \
  --user=$UID \
  -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-Xmx1g" \
  -v "$(pwd)/data":/data \
  --rm \
  ghcr.io/onthegomap/planetiler:latest \
  --download \
  --minzoom=0 \
  --maxzoom=14 \
  --tile_compression=none \
  --area=monaco \
  --output /data/monaco.mbtiles
```

Monaco is small, so this finishes in a few minutes. Any other [Geofabrik extract name](<https://download.geofabrik.de/>) works as `--area` the same way, with larger downloads and longer runs.

## Get a style

A style only works with data in the schema it was written for. Planetiler produced tiles in the OpenMapTiles schema, so you need an OpenMapTiles style. You will use [OSM Bright](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style>). [Positron](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/positron-gl-style>), [Dark Matter](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/dark-matter-gl-style>), [MapTiler Basic](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/maptiler-basic-gl-style>), and [OSM Liberty](<https://github.com/maputnik/osm-liberty>) are alternatives.

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style.git
mkdir --parents styles
cp osm-bright-gl-style/style.json styles/basemap.json
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Attribution**
>
> Your map must display [`© OpenMapTiles`](<https://openmaptiles.org/>) and [`© OpenStreetMap contributors`](<https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright>). The tile archive built above carries this attribution in its metadata, and MapLibre displays it automatically.

## Get the fonts the style uses

OSM Bright labels text with `Noto Sans Regular`, `Noto Sans Bold`, and `Noto Sans Italic`. Martin generates the glyph ranges MapLibre asks for [directly from `.ttf`/`.otf` files](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-fonts/index.md>), so all you need are the font files themselves:

```bash
mkdir --parents fonts
curl -L -o fonts/NotoSans-Regular.ttf https://github.com/notofonts/notofonts.github.io/raw/main/fonts/NotoSans/full/ttf/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
curl -L -o fonts/NotoSans-Bold.ttf https://github.com/notofonts/notofonts.github.io/raw/main/fonts/NotoSans/full/ttf/NotoSans-Bold.ttf
curl -L -o fonts/NotoSans-Italic.ttf https://github.com/notofonts/notofonts.github.io/raw/main/fonts/NotoSans/full/ttf/NotoSans-Italic.ttf
```

Martin publishes each font under the name embedded in the file. Here that is `Noto Sans Regular`, `Noto Sans Bold`, and `Noto Sans Italic`, exactly the names the style asks for.

## Get the icons the style uses

The style repository ships its icons as SVG files. Martin [generates the spritesheet and index from an SVG directory on the fly](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-sprites/index.md>), so copying the folder is all that is needed:

```bash
cp -r osm-bright-gl-style/icons icons
```

The directory name becomes the sprite ID, so these will be served under `/sprite/icons`.

## Point the style at your server

The copied style still references the original author's tile, glyph, and sprite servers. Open `styles/basemap.json` and change three values to point at the Martin instance you are about to start:

| Key | New value |
| --- | --- |
| `sources.openmaptiles.url` | `http://localhost:3000/monaco` |
| `glyphs` | `http://localhost:3000/font/{fontstack}/{range}` |
| `sprite` | `http://localhost:3000/sprite/icons` |

The `sources` URL is the [TileJSON endpoint](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using/index.md>) of the `monaco` archive. The `{fontstack}` and `{range}` placeholders are filled in by MapLibre when it requests glyph ranges.

## Run Martin

Everything is in place, so serve all four resources with one command:

```bash
martin data/monaco.mbtiles --font fonts --sprite icons --style styles
```

Check [http://localhost:3000/catalog](<http://localhost:3000/catalog>) to see the `monaco` tile source, the three fonts, the `icons` sprite, and the `basemap` style. For more control over what is published and how, see the [configuration file](<https://maplibre.org/martin/config-file/index.md>) documentation. `--save-config` converts the command line above into a config file to grow from.

## View the map

Save this as `index.html` in the working directory and open it in your browser:

index.html

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>My self-hosted map</title>
  <script src="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@^5/dist/maplibre-gl.js"></script>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@^5/dist/maplibre-gl.css">
  <style>
    html, body, #map { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div id="map"></div>
  <script>
    const map = new maplibregl.Map({
      container: 'map',
      style: 'http://localhost:3000/style/basemap',
      center: [7.4266, 43.7396],
      zoom: 14,
    });
    map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl());
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

![The finished self-hosted basemap of Monaco](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/selfhosted-basemap.png>)

The page loads the style from Martin, and the style pulls the tiles, glyphs, and sprites from Martin. The complete map is served from your machine.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Small extracts may not contain every layer the style references. Monaco has no aerodrome, so the browser console warns that the `aerodrome_label` source layer does not exist. The map renders fine regardless.

## Where to go from here

- [Overlay your own data from PostGIS on this basemap](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-basemap-postgis/index.md>)
- Put Martin behind a [reverse proxy](<https://maplibre.org/martin/run-with-reverse-proxy/index.md>) for TLS, caching, and a public hostname, and update the three URLs in the style to the public one
- Pre-generate tiles for offline use or for seeding a cache with [`martin cp`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-cp/index.md>)
- [Render the style into raster tiles server-side](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/index.md>)

# Map renderer specific

Martin can serve tiles to a variety of map rendering libraries. Below are guides for integrating Martin with some of the most popular renderers:

- [MapLibre GL JS](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-maplibre/index.md>)
- [Leaflet](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-leaflet/index.md>)
- [deck.gl](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-deck-gl/index.md>)
- [Mapbox GL JS](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-mapbox/index.md>)
- [OpenLayers](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-openlayers/index.md>)

# Using with MapLibre

[MapLibre](<https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/>) is an Open-source JavaScript library for showing maps on a website. MapLibre can accept [MVT vector tiles](<https://github.com/mapbox/vector-tile-spec>) generated by Martin, and applies [a style](<https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/>) to them to draw a map using Web GL.

You can add a layer to the map and specify Martin [TileJSON](<https://github.com/mapbox/tilejson-spec>) endpoint as a vector source URL. You should also specify a `source-layer` property. For [Table Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-tables/index.md>) it is `{table_name}` by default.

```js
map.addLayer({
    id: 'points',
    type: 'circle',
    source: {
        type: 'vector',
        url: 'http://localhost:3000/points'
    },
    'source-layer': 'points',
    paint: {
        'circle-color': 'red'
    },
});
```

```js
map.addSource('rpc', {
    type: 'vector',
    url: `http://localhost:3000/function_zxy_query`
});
map.addLayer({
    id: 'points',
    type: 'circle',
    source: 'rpc',
    'source-layer': 'function_zxy_query',
    paint: {
        'circle-color': 'blue'
    },
});
```

You can also combine multiple sources into one source with [Composite Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-composite/index.md>). Each source in a composite source can be accessed with its `{source_name}` as a `source-layer` property.

```js
map.addSource('points', {
    type: 'vector',
    url: `http://0.0.0.0:3000/points1,points2`
});

map.addLayer({
    id: 'red_points',
    type: 'circle',
    source: 'points',
    'source-layer': 'points1',
    paint: {
        'circle-color': 'red'
    }
});

map.addLayer({
    id: 'blue_points',
    type: 'circle',
    source: 'points',
    'source-layer': 'points2',
    paint: {
        'circle-color': 'blue'
    }
});
```

# Using with Leaflet

[Leaflet](<https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet>) is the leading open-source JavaScript library for mobile-friendly interactive maps.

You can add vector tiles using [`Leaflet.VectorGrid`](<https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet.VectorGrid>) plugin. You must initialize a [`VectorGrid.Protobuf`](<https://leaflet.github.io/Leaflet.VectorGrid/vectorgrid-api-docs.html#vectorgrid-protobuf>) with a URL template, just like in `L.TileLayers`. The difference is that you should define the styling for all the features.

```js
L.vectorGrid
  .protobuf('http://localhost:3000/points/{z}/{x}/{y}', {
    vectorTileLayerStyles: {
      'points': {
        color: 'red',
        fill: true
      }
    }
  })
  .addTo(map);
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Style serving is specific to [maplibre](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-maplibre/index.md>) or [deck.gl](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-deck-gl/index.md>).

# Using with deck.gl

[deck.gl](<https://deck.gl/>) is a WebGL-powered framework for visual exploratory data analysis of large datasets.

You can add vector tiles using [MVTLayer](<https://deck.gl/docs/api-reference/geo-layers/mvt-layer>). MVTLayer `data` property defines the remote data for the MVT layer. It can be

- `String`: Either a URL template or a [TileJSON](<https://github.com/mapbox/tilejson-spec>) URL.
- `Array`: an array of URL templates. It allows to balance the requests across different tile endpoints. For example, if you define an array with 4 urls and 16 tiles need to be loaded, each endpoint is responsible to server 16/4 tiles.
- `JSON`: A valid [TileJSON object](<https://github.com/mapbox/tilejson-spec/tree/master/2.2.0>).

```js
const pointsLayer = new MVTLayer({
  data: 'http://localhost:3000/points',
  pointRadiusUnits: 'pixels',
  getRadius: 5,
  getFillColor: [230, 0, 0]
});

const deckgl = new DeckGL({
  container: 'map',
  mapStyle: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/dark-matter-gl-style/style.json',
  initialViewState: {
    latitude: 0,
    longitude: 0,
    zoom: 1
  },
  layers: [pointsLayer]
});
```

# Using with Mapbox

[Mapbox GL JS](<https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gl-js>) is a JavaScript library for interactive, customizable vector maps on the web. Mapbox GL JS v1.x was open source, and it was forked as MapLibre, so [using Martin with Mapbox is similar to MapLibre](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-maplibre/index.md>). Mapbox GL JS can accept [MVT vector tiles](<https://github.com/mapbox/vector-tile-spec>) generated by Martin, and applies [a style](<https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/>) to them to draw a map using Web GL.

You can add a layer to the map and specify Martin TileJSON endpoint as a vector source URL. You should also specify a `source-layer` property. For [Table Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-tables/index.md>) it is `{table_name}` by default.

```js
map.addLayer({
    id: 'points',
    type: 'circle',
    source: {
        type: 'vector',
        url: 'http://localhost:3000/points'
    },
    'source-layer': 'points',
    paint: {
        'circle-color': 'red'
    }
});
```

# Using with OpenLayers

[OpenLayers](<https://github.com/openlayers/openlayers>) is an open source library for creating interactive maps on the web. Similar to [MapLibre GL JS](<https://maplibre.org/>), it can also display image and vector map tiles served by Martin Tile Server.

You can integrate tile services from `martin` and `OpenLayers` with its [VectorTileLayer](<https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_layer_VectorTile-VectorTileLayer.html>). Here is an example to add `MixPoints` vector tile source to an OpenLayers map.

```js
const layer = new VectorTileLayer({
    source: new VectorTileSource({
        format: new MVT(),
        url: 'http://0.0.0.0:3000/MixPoints/{z}/{x}/{y}',
        maxZoom: 14,
    }),
});
map.addLayer(layer);
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Style serving is specific to [maplibre](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-maplibre/>) or [deck.gl](<https://maplibre.org/martin/using-with-deck-gl/>).

# Tile source specific

Some sources for tiles are harder to setup than others. Below are setup instructions for some common data sources:

- [Hosted PostgreSQL](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipes/index.md>)
- [Setting up a basemap and overlaying data](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-basemap-postgis/index.md>)
- [Serving NAIP imagery from S3 with a tile index](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-cog-naip/index.md>)

# Hosted PostgreSQL

Some providers of PostgreSQL databases require additional configuration to work with Martin. We try to provide a guide for each provider, but we may not cover all of them.

## Using with DigitalOcean PostgreSQL

You can use Martin with [Managed PostgreSQL from DigitalOcean](<https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-postgresql/>) with PostGIS extension

First, you need to download the CA certificate and get your cluster connection string from the [dashboard](<https://cloud.digitalocean.com/databases>). After that, you can use the connection string and the CA certificate to connect to the database

```bash
martin --ca-root-file ./ca-certificate.crt \
       postgres://user:password@host:port/db?sslmode=require
```

## Using with Heroku PostgreSQL

You can use Martin with [Managed PostgreSQL from Heroku](<https://www.heroku.com/postgres>) with the PostGIS extension

```bash
heroku pg:psql -a APP_NAME -c 'create extension postgis'
```

Set the environment variables Heroku [suggests for psql](<https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-postgres-via-mtls#step-2-configure-environment-variables>) and pass them to Martin on the command line.

```bash
export DATABASE_URL=$(heroku config:get DATABASE_URL -a APP_NAME)
export PGSSLCERT=DIRECTORY/PREFIXpostgresql.crt
export PGSSLKEY=DIRECTORY/PREFIXpostgresql.key
export PGSSLROOTCERT=DIRECTORY/PREFIXroot.crt

martin --ssl-cert "$PGSSLCERT" --ssl-key "$PGSSLKEY" --ca-root-file "$PGSSLROOTCERT" "$DATABASE_URL"
```

You may also be able to validate SSL certificate with an explicit sslmode, e.g.

```bash
export DATABASE_URL="$(heroku config:get DATABASE_URL -a APP_NAME)?sslmode=verify-ca"
```

# Setting up a Basemap and Overlaying Points from PostGIS

You commonly have some semi-proprietary datasource which you want to overlay onto another. This guide shows how to generate a basemap using [Planetiler](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler/>) from [OSM](<https://osm.org>) and overlay custom points from a [PostGIS](<https://postgis.net/>) database. See here for a discussion on the [pros and cons of this/alternative data sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-tiles/index.md>).

## Prerequisites

You need the following already installed:

- [Docker](<https://docker.io>)
- [Martin binary](<https://maplibre.org/martin/installation/index.md>)

## Generate an MBTiles basemap with Planetiler

There are multiple ways to generate a tile archive. For semi-static tile archives, we think using [Planetiler](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler/>) to build MBtiles archives using [OpenMapTiles](<https://openmaptiles.org/>) is a good starting point.

**🤔 *Why do I need a tool to convert OSM to mbtiles in the first place?* (click to expand)**

The reason you need a tool to build vector tilesets from OpenStreetMap is that the data in OpenStreetMap is - not following a specific schema, - nor pre-tiled into \`x\`/\`y\`/\`z\` chunks.

**🤔 *What is up with MBtiles and OpenMapTiles* (click to expand)**

Good question. MBtiles is the archive format. Think of a sqlite database storing the data you need a chunk (\`x\`/\`y\`/\`z\`) of the world. See the comparison \[pmtiles vs. mbtiles\](sources-tiles/index.md) for discussions on the pros and cons of this/alternative formats. But how does the data in the archive look like? This is where the vector tile schema comes in: \[OpenMapTiles\](https://openmaptiles.org/) defines which layers are included in the served data and how they are aggregated. \[OpenMapTiles\](https://openmaptiles.org/) does have an attribution requirement. You will need to have \[\`© OpenMapTiles\`\](https://openmaptiles.org/) at the bottom of your map. See \[Shortbread\](https://shortbread-tiles.org/) for a newer, but less mature alternative if you want to read more.

Below command downloads a tile archive at `data/monaco.mbtiles` for monaco.

Please refer to [Planetilers documentation](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler/>) on different download options.

```bash
mkdir --parents data
docker run \
  --user=$UID \
  -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-Xmx1g" \
  -v "$(pwd)/data":/data \
  --rm \
  ghcr.io/onthegomap/planetiler:latest \
  --download \
  --minzoom=0 \
  --maxzoom=14 \
  --tile_compression=none \
  --area=monaco \
  --output /data/monaco.mbtiles
```

## Loading data into a PostGIS database

### Run PostGIS

First, you need a running [postGIS](<https://postgis.net>) instance.

```bash
docker run \
  --name some-postgis \
  --env POSTGRES_PASSWORD=mypass \
  --publish 5432:5432 \
  --detach \
  postgis/postgis
```

### Import Points into PostGIS

Then you need to add geometries to the PostGIS database. This is possible via multiple ways, such as [`osm2pgsql` for adding specific, updatable OSM data](<https://osm2pgsql.org/>) or in the programming language of your choice via postgres' various database connectors.

```bash
docker exec some-postgis psql --dbname postgres --username postgres --command \
  "CREATE TABLE where_yachts_can_be_looked_at ("\
  "  title TEXT NOT NULL, "\
  "  subtitle TEXT NOT NULL, "\
  "  location GEOMETRY(Point, 4326) NOT NULL);"

docker exec some-postgis psql --dbname postgres --username postgres --command \
  "INSERT INTO where_yachts_can_be_looked_at (title, subtitle, location) VALUES ( "\
  "  'Port Hercules', "\
  "  'Great view of superyachts docked in the iconic harbor.', "\
  "  ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(7.424789, 43.735217), 4326));"
```

## Serving tiles with Martin

Now serve the content of [mbtiles](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-mbtiles/index.md>) and the [postgis database](<https://maplibre.org/martin/pg-connections/index.md>).

If you want more precise options what things are published how, please see the [configuration file](<https://maplibre.org/martin/config-file/index.md>) or [cli documentation](<https://maplibre.org/martin/run-with-cli/index.md>). By default, Martin shares every servable postgres [table, view](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-tables/index.md>) and [function](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-functions/index.md>).

```bash
martin data/monaco.mbtiles postgres://postgres:mypass@localhost:5432/postgres
```

You can now see the catalog of available things here: [`http://localhost:3000/catalog`](<http://localhost:3000/catalog>) The tilejson endpoint of both tilesets is [`http://localhost:3000/monaco,where_yachts_can_be_looked_at`](<http://localhost:3000/monaco,where_yachts_can_be_looked_at>)

## Using in Maputnik to style a map

Due to CORS, you CANNOT use the website [https://maplibre.org/maputnik/](<https://maplibre.org/maputnik/>) without further setup. Once the tiles are deployed behind https, this can be used.

To get a local version of maputnik, run

```bash
docker run -it --rm -p 8888:80 ghcr.io/maplibre/maputnik:main
```

Maputnik is now online, so load martins tiles into it.

1. Visit [`http://localhost:8888`](<http://localhost:8888>)
2. You first need a style:
3. Click `Open` ![where in the UI the "Open" button can be found](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/open.png>)
4. Select a style you like (this guide chooses `Maptiler Basic`) ![how to select a style](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/select-style.png>)
5. You now have a style using Maptilers' (**NOT martins**) data. You need to change its datasource to use the tiles you just published:
6. Click `Data Sources` ![how to change the datasource](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/change-datasource.png>)
7. And add the tilejson from above `http://localhost:3000/monaco,where_yachts_can_be_looked_at`: ![how to add the tilejson](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/add-tilejson.png>)
8. Now, zoom into monaco: ![where monaco is on a map](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/zoom-into-monaco.png>)
9. And finally, add a circle layer for the yachts:
10. Click `Add Layer` ![add a circle layer](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/add-layer.png>)
11. Configure the layer as follows: ![add a circle layer](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/configure-layer.png>)
12. And style it as: ![add a circle layer](<https://maplibre.org/martin/images/maputnik/add-yachts-layer.png>)

    **json configuration (click to expand)**

    ```json
    {
      "id": "where_yachts_can_be_looked_at",
      "type": "circle",
      "source": "openmaptiles",
      "source-layer": "where_yachts_can_be_looked_at",
      "paint": {
        "circle-color": "rgba(255, 7, 103, 1)",
        "circle-blur": 0.2,
        "circle-radius": {
          "stops": [
            [13, 1],
            [15, 300],
            [20, 2000]
          ]
        },
        "circle-opacity": {
          "stops": [[13.5, 0], [14, 0.4]]
        }
      },
      "minzoom": 13
    }
    ```

# Serving NAIP aerial imagery from S3 with a tile index

The [National Agriculture Imagery Program](<https://registry.opendata.aws/naip/>) (NAIP) publishes aerial imagery of the United States as COGs in the `naip-visualization` S3 bucket: one file per USGS quarter-quadrangle, each in its own UTM zone, overlapping its neighbors. This guide serves all of California 2020 as one Martin source with a [tile index](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-cog-files/index.md#imagery-listed-by-a-tile-index>), and shows the Bay Area on a MapLibre map with [OpenFreeMap](<https://openfreemap.org>) roads on top.

## Prerequisites

- [Martin](<https://maplibre.org/martin/installation/index.md>), built with the `cog` feature (on by default)
- The [AWS CLI](<https://aws.amazon.com/cli/>) and the [GDAL](<https://gdal.org>) command line tools, for `ogr2ogr`
- AWS credentials allowed to read `s3://naip-visualization`. The bucket is **requester pays**: every request is billed to your AWS account, so a request without `--request-payer requester` (or Martin's `aws_request_payer: true`) is denied.

Check your access with a 4 KB range read:

```bash
aws s3api get-object --bucket naip-visualization \
  --key ca/2020/60cm/rgb/37122/m_3712213_nw_10_060_20200524.tif \
  --request-payer requester --range bytes=0-4095 header.tif
```

## Build the tile index

Each state and year comes with an index of its own: a shapefile with the footprint of every quarter-quadrangle, e.g. `ca/2020/60cm/index/NAIP_20_CA.shp`. Its `FileName` is not quite the file's key, though: it lacks the folder, and ends in an extra date, the version date. For a few files, its image date is also a day off from the key's. So the index is joined to a listing of the files by their names up to the date, which gives every footprint its real key:

```bash
export AWS_REGION=us-west-2 AWS_REQUEST_PAYER=requester

# Every file the bucket has, with its name up to the date, e.g. `m_3712213_nw_10_060`.
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket naip-visualization --request-payer requester \
  --prefix ca/2020/60cm/rgb/ --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text | tr '\t' '\n' \
  | awk -F/ 'BEGIN { print "key,qq" } /\.tif$/ { print $0 "," substr($NF, 1, 19) }' > files.csv

# The bucket's footprints and the listing, side by side.
ogr2ogr -f GPKG -nln footprints work.gpkg /vsis3/naip-visualization/ca/2020/60cm/index/NAIP_20_CA.shp
ogr2ogr -update -nln files work.gpkg files.csv

# One row per file: its footprint, and where to read it.
ogr2ogr -f GPKG -nln naip naip.gpkg work.gpkg -dialect SQLite -sql \
  "SELECT '/vsis3/naip-visualization/' || f.key AS location, p.geom
   FROM footprints p JOIN files f ON f.qq = substr(p.FileName, 1, 19)"
```

This takes about 20 seconds for the 11,076 files of California 2020, and reads no file but the index. For another state or year, list its `index/` folder for the shapefile's name.

> [!TIP]
>
> Imagery without an index of its own can be indexed with `gdaltindex -f GPKG -t_srs EPSG:4326`, which reads the header of every file.

## Configure Martin

config.yaml

```yaml
cog:
  # An AWS SDK profile with read access to the bucket; any other way of passing credentials works too.
  profile: naip
  aws_region: us-west-2
  # The bucket is requester pays.
  aws_request_payer: true
  tile_index:
    naip:
      path: naip.gpkg
      minzoom: 14
      maxzoom: 19
```

```bash
martin --config config.yaml
curl -o tile.png http://localhost:3000/naip/18/41886/101282
```

The first tile of an area takes a few seconds while Martin opens the files; later tiles reuse them. Zooms outside `minzoom` to `maxzoom` are answered with `404` without reading from S3.

## Show it on a map

This page shows the Golden Gate Bridge at zoom 18 with the roads and labels of OpenFreeMap on top, motorways to secondary roads in pink. `hash: true` keeps the map position in the URL, e.g. `#14/37.93/-122.69`.

Save it as `index.html` and serve it over HTTP, e.g. with `python3 -m http.server 8000`, then open [http://localhost:8000](<http://localhost:8000>).

index.html

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>NAIP z18 demo</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.14.0/dist/maplibre-gl.css">
<style>
  :root { --bg: #000; --fg: #fff; --accent: #ff4fa3; }
  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); font: 13px/1.4 system-ui, sans-serif; }
  #map { position: absolute; inset: 0; }
  #panel { position: absolute; top: 12px; left: 12px; background: var(--bg); border: 2px solid var(--accent);
           border-radius: 2px; padding: 8px 10px; z-index: 1; min-width: 230px; }
  #panel b { color: var(--accent); }
  #panel label { display: block; margin-top: 6px; cursor: pointer; }
  #panel button { margin: 6px 6px 0 0; background: var(--accent); color: #000; border: 0; border-radius: 2px;
                  padding: 4px 8px; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; }
  code { color: var(--accent); }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div id="map"></div>
<div id="panel">
  <b>NAIP CA 2020 / martin tile_index</b><br>
  source <code>localhost:3000/naip</code><br>
  z <code id="z"></code> naip tile <code id="tile"></code>
  <label><input type="checkbox" id="ofm" checked> OpenFreeMap roads + labels</label>
  <button data-go="-122.4783,37.8199">Golden Gate</button>
  <button data-go="-122.3937,37.7955">Ferry Building</button>
  <button data-go="-122.4230,37.8267">Alcatraz</button>
  <button data-go="-122.2585,37.8024">Lake Merritt</button>
</div>
<script type="module">
import { Map, NavigationControl } from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.14.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs";

const CENTER = [-122.4783, 37.8199];
const BIG_ROADS = ["motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary"];

// MapLibre line widths are pixels of a 512 px tile world; at this latitude a meter is this many px at zoom z.
const pxPerMeter = z => (512 * 2 ** z) / (40075016.686 * Math.cos(CENTER[1] * Math.PI / 180));
const meters = m => ["interpolate", ["exponential", 2], ["zoom"], 10, m * pxPerMeter(10), 22, m * pxPerMeter(22)];

const BOUNDS = [[-122.65, 37.60], [-122.10, 38.00]];
const bigRoad = ["in", ["get", "class"], ["literal", BIG_ROADS]];
const ofmLayers = ["ofm-roads", "ofm-big-roads", "ofm-road-names", "ofm-places"];

const map = new Map({
  container: "map",
  center: CENTER,
  zoom: 18,
  hash: true,
  minZoom: 14,
  maxZoom: 19,
  maxBounds: BOUNDS,
  style: {
    version: 8,
    glyphs: "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
    sources: {
      naip: { type: "raster", tiles: ["http://localhost:3000/naip/{z}/{x}/{y}"], tileSize: 256,
              minzoom: 14, maxzoom: 19, attribution: "NAIP 2020 via martin" },
      ofm: { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet",
             attribution: "<a href=\"https://openfreemap.org\">OpenFreeMap</a> &copy; OpenMapTiles" },
    },
    layers: [
      { id: "bg", type: "background", paint: { "background-color": "#111" } },
      { id: "naip", type: "raster", source: "naip" },
      {
        id: "ofm-roads", type: "line", source: "ofm", "source-layer": "transportation",
        filter: ["!", bigRoad],
        paint: { "line-color": "#ffffff", "line-opacity": 0.45, "line-width": ["interpolate", ["linear"], ["zoom"], 14, 0.5, 20, 2] },
      },
      {
        id: "ofm-big-roads", type: "line", source: "ofm", "source-layer": "transportation",
        filter: bigRoad,
        layout: { "line-cap": "round", "line-join": "round" },
        paint: { "line-color": "#ff4fa3", "line-opacity": 0.9, "line-width": ["interpolate", ["exponential", 2], ["zoom"], 14, 2, 22, 3 * pxPerMeter(22)] },
      },
      {
        id: "ofm-road-names", type: "symbol", source: "ofm", "source-layer": "transportation_name",
        layout: { "symbol-placement": "line", "text-field": ["coalesce", ["get", "name:en"], ["get", "name"]],
                  "text-font": ["Noto Sans Regular"], "text-size": 14 },
        paint: { "text-color": "#fff", "text-halo-color": "#000", "text-halo-width": 1.5 },
      },
      {
        id: "ofm-places", type: "symbol", source: "ofm", "source-layer": "place",
        layout: { "text-field": ["coalesce", ["get", "name:en"], ["get", "name"]],
                  "text-font": ["Noto Sans Regular"], "text-size": 15 },
        paint: { "text-color": "#ff4fa3", "text-halo-color": "#000", "text-halo-width": 1.5 },
      },
    ],
  },
});
map.addControl(new NavigationControl(), "top-right");

// The NAIP tile MapLibre requests at the center: its tiles are 256 px, so one zoom above the map's 512 px zoom.
function update() {
  const z = Math.min(Math.floor(map.getZoom()) + 1, map.getSource("naip").maxzoom), c = map.getCenter(), n = 2 ** z;
  const x = Math.floor((c.lng + 180) / 360 * n);
  const r = c.lat * Math.PI / 180;
  const y = Math.floor((1 - Math.asinh(Math.tan(r)) / Math.PI) / 2 * n);
  document.getElementById("z").textContent = map.getZoom().toFixed(1);
  document.getElementById("tile").textContent = `${z}/${x}/${y}`;
}
map.on("move", update);
map.on("load", update);

const visible = on => (on ? "visible" : "none");
document.getElementById("ofm").onchange = e =>
  ofmLayers.forEach(id => map.setLayoutProperty(id, "visibility", visible(e.target.checked)));
document.querySelectorAll("[data-go]").forEach(b => b.onclick = () =>
  map.flyTo({ center: b.dataset.go.split(",").map(Number), zoom: 18 }));
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

# Building a basemap from OpenStreetMap

This builds a basemap tileset from an [OpenStreetMap](<https://www.openstreetmap.org/>) extract, with the layers and attributes using the [Shortbread](<https://shortbread-tiles.org/>) schema, so that [VersaTiles styles](<https://github.com/versatiles-org/versatiles-style>) can draw them. The configuration is a port of Planetiler's [`shortbread.yml`](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler/blob/main/planetiler-custommap/src/main/resources/samples/shortbread.yml>), and Martin's tests use the 67 examples of its `shortbread.spec.yml`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> **More information on the config used**
>
> The `osm` section is described in [OpenStreetMap PBF Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-osm/index.md>), the `shapefile` section in [Shapefile Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-shapefile/index.md>).

One layer differs from Planetiler's: `boundaries` also takes the member ways of `admin_level` 2 and 4 boundary relations, many of which have no tags of their own, with the lowest `admin_level` of the way and its relations. Planetiler's `shortbread.yml` reads only tagged ways and leaves this as a TODO. The configuration reads the relations through [relation membership](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-osm/index.md#relation-membership>).

1. Download an extract, for example Berlin from [Geofabrik](<https://download.geofabrik.de/>), and the ocean polygons of the whole world from [osmdata.openstreetmap.de](<https://osmdata.openstreetmap.de/data/water-polygons.html>), about 900 MB:

   ```bash
   curl -LO https://download.geofabrik.de/europe/germany/berlin-latest.osm.pbf
   curl -LO https://osmdata.openstreetmap.de/download/water-polygons-split-3857.zip
   ```
2. Save this as `shortbread.yaml`, next to both downloads:

   > **shortbread.yaml**
   >
   > ```yaml
   > shapefile:
   >   sources:
   >     ocean:
   >       path: water-polygons-split-3857.zip
   >       maxzoom: 14
   >       layers:
   >         ocean:
   >           geometry: polygon
   >           attributes: []
   > osm:
   >   sources:
   >     shortbread:
   >       path: berlin-latest.osm.pbf

   >             tourism: >-
   >               tourism in ['artwork', 'alpine_hut', 'bed_and_breakfast', 'camp_site', 'caravan_site', 'chalet',
   >               'guest_house', 'hostel', 'hotel', 'information', 'motel', 'picnic_site', 'theme_park', 'viewpoint',
   >               'zoo'] ? tourism : null
   >             shop: >-
   >               shop in ['alcohol', 'bakery', 'beauty', 'beverages', 'bicycle', 'books', 'butcher', 'car', 'chemist',
   >               'clothes', 'computer', 'convenience', 'department_store', 'doityourself', 'dry_cleaning', 'florist',
   >               'furniture', 'garden_centre', 'general', 'gift', 'greengrocer', 'hairdresser', 'hardware', 'jewelry',
   >               'kiosk', 'laundry', 'mall', 'mobile_phone', 'newsagent', 'optician', 'outdoor', 'shoes', 'sports',
   >               'stationery', 'supermarket', 'toys', 'travel_agency', 'video'] ? shop : null
   >             man_made: >-
   >               man_made in ['lighthouse', 'surveillance', 'tower', 'wastewater_plant', 'water_well', 'water_works',
   >               'watermill', 'windmill'] ? man_made : null
   >             historic: >-
   >               historic in ['archaeological_site', 'battlefield', 'castle', 'fort', 'memorial', 'monument', 'ruins',
   >               'wayside_cross', 'wayside_shrine'] ? historic : null
   >             emergency: "emergency in ['defibrillator', 'fire_hydrant', 'phone'] ? emergency : null"
   >             highway: "highway == 'emergency_access_point' ? highway : null"
   >             office: "office == 'diplomatic' ? office : null"
   >             name: name
   >             name_en: "feature['name:en']"
   >             name_de: "feature['name:de']"
   >             housename: "feature['addr:housename']"
   >             housenumber: "feature['addr:housenumber']"
   >             cuisine: "amenity in ['restaurant', 'fast_food', 'pub', 'bar', 'cafe'] ? cuisine : null"
   >             sport: "leisure in ['pitch', 'sports_centre'] ? sport : null"
   >             vending: "amenity == 'vending_machine' ? vending : null"
   >             information: "tourism == 'information' ? information : null"
   >             "tower:type": "man_made == 'tower' ? feature['tower:type'] : null"
   >             religion: "amenity == 'place_of_worship' ? religion : null"
   >             denomination: "amenity == 'place_of_worship' ? denomination : null"
   >             "recycling:glass_bottles": "amenity == 'recycling' ? feature['recycling:glass_bottles'] == 'yes' : null"
   >             "recycling:paper": "amenity == 'recycling' ? feature['recycling:paper'] == 'yes' : null"
   >             "recycling:clothes": "amenity == 'recycling' ? feature['recycling:clothes'] == 'yes' : null"
   >             "recycling:scrap_metal": "amenity == 'recycling' ? feature['recycling:scrap_metal'] == 'yes' : null"
   >             atm: "amenity == 'bank' ? atm == 'yes' : null"
   > ```
3. Generate the tileset of the extract's area. The ocean polygons cover the whole world, so without `--bbox` the tileset does too:

   ```bash
   martin cp --mode bulk --config shortbread.yaml --output-file berlin.mbtiles --format mvt --max-zoom 14 \
     --bbox 13.08,52.33,13.77,52.68
   ```
4. Serve it, and point a style's `versatiles-shortbread` source at `http://localhost:3000/berlin`:

   ```bash
   martin berlin.mbtiles
   ```

| Extract | PBF | Features | Tiles | Time | Memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Berlin, 2026-11-11 | 100 MB | 1,646,140 | 889 | 15.3 s | 6.0 GB |
| Germany, 2026-11-11 | 4.9 GB | 75,149,336 | 251,613 | 2m 54s | 19.1 GB |

Measured on 24 threads, with the extract and the ocean polygons of 2026-11-14 in the page cache, each run with the `--bbox` of its extract. 3 s of each run unpack the ocean polygons. With `--bbox`, Martin keeps whole tiles, so the ocean polygons of the whole world go into the low-zoom tiles: they take Berlin from 3 s to 15 s.

# Building OpenMapTiles from OpenStreetMap

This recipe builds a basemap from an [OpenStreetMap](<https://www.openstreetmap.org/>) extract with the 16 layers of the [OpenMapTiles schema](<https://openmaptiles.org/schema/>). Styles made for OpenMapTiles, such as [OSM Bright](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style>) and [Positron](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/positron-gl-style>) can then draw this data.

The configuration is a port of [Planetiler's OpenMapTiles profile](<https://github.com/openmaptiles/planetiler-openmaptiles>). It keeps Planetiler's zooms, minimum sizes, buffers, label grids, merges and draw orders. It reads only OpenStreetMap and the ocean polygons of the whole world. It leaves out what Planetiler takes from Natural Earth and Wikidata, see [How it differs](<#how-it-differs-from-planetilers-openmaptiles>).

The configuration uses an `osm` section, described in [OpenStreetMap PBF Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-osm/index.md>), a `shapefile` section, described in [Shapefile Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-shapefile/index.md>), and the layer keys of [Table Source Layers](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md>).

## Build the tileset

1. Download an extract, for example Berlin from [Geofabrik](<https://download.geofabrik.de/>), and the ocean polygons of the whole world from [osmdata.openstreetmap.de](<https://osmdata.openstreetmap.de/data/water-polygons.html>), about 900 MB:

   ```bash
   curl -LO https://download.geofabrik.de/europe/germany/berlin-latest.osm.pbf
   curl -LO https://osmdata.openstreetmap.de/download/water-polygons-split-3857.zip
   ```
2. Save this as `openmaptiles.yaml`, next to both downloads:

   > **openmaptiles.yaml**
   >
   > ```yaml
   > shapefile:
   >   sources:
   >     ocean:
   >       path: water-polygons-split-3857.zip
   >       maxzoom: 14
   >       layers:
   >         ocean:
   >           layer: water
   >           geometry: polygon
   >           buffer: 64
   >           attributes:
   >             class: { value: ocean }
   >           merge_polygons:
   >             - { maxzoom: 13, min_area: 1 }
   >             - { minzoom: 14, min_area: 0.0625 }
   > osm:
   >   sources:

   >         - rank

   >         - religion

   >         - sac_scale
   >         - service
   >         - shop
   >         - sport
   >         - station
   >         - surface
   >         - toll

   >       relations:

   >           where: >-
   >             type == 'boundary' && boundary == 'administrative' && admin_level != null
   >           tags: [admin_level, name, disputed, dispute, border_status, disputed_by, claimed_by]
   >         route:

   >             type == 'route' && route in ['road', 'hiking'] && (network != null || feature['osmc:symbol'] !=

   >           tags: [network, ref, name, colour, "ref:colour", "osmc:symbol"]
   >         river:
   >           where: "waterway == 'river' && name != null"

   >         # water: the ocean comes from the shapefile source above, at every zoom

   >           layer: water

   >           buffer: 64

   >           min_size: 1

   >           maxzoom: "area('km2') >= 25 ? 5 : 0"
   >           where: "natural == 'water' && (water == null || water in ['lake', 'reservoir', 'lagoon']) && covered != 'yes'"
   >           attributes:
   >             id: osm_id
   >             intermittent: "intermittent != null && !(intermittent in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 1 : 0"
   >             class: { value: lake }
   >         water:
   >           geometry: polygon
   >           buffer: 64
   >           minzoom: 6
   >           maxzoom: 11
   >           simplify: 0.1
   >           min_size: 2
   >           where: &water_where >-
   >             (landuse in ['reservoir', 'basin', 'salt_pond'] || leisure == 'swimming_pool' || natural in
   >             ['water', 'spring'] || waterway == 'dock' || water in ['river', 'stream', 'canal', 'ditch',
   >             'drain', 'pond', 'basin', 'wastewater']) && covered != 'yes' && natural != 'bay'
   >           attributes: &water_attributes
   >             id: osm_id
   >             intermittent: "intermittent != null && !(intermittent in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 1 : 0"
   >             brunnel:
   >               expr: >-
   >                 bridge != null && !(bridge in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 'bridge' : tunnel != null &&
   >                 !(tunnel in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 'tunnel' : null
   >               minzoom: 12
   >             class: >-
   >               waterway == 'dock' ? 'dock' : water in ['river', 'stream', 'canal', 'ditch', 'drain'] ?
   >               'river' : water in ['pond', 'basin', 'wastewater', 'salt_pond'] ? 'pond' : leisure ==
   >               'swimming_pool' ? 'swimming_pool' : 'lake'
   >         water_z12:
   >           layer: water
   >           geometry: polygon
   >           buffer: 64
   >           minzoom: 12
   >           min_size_at_maxzoom: 0.0625
   >           where: *water_where
   >           attributes: *water_attributes
   >         # waterway: river relation members at z6-8, ways from z9
   >         waterway_relations:
   >           layer: waterway
   >           geometry: line
   >           buffer: 1024
   >           minzoom: 6
   >           maxzoom: 8
   >           simplify: 0.1
   >           min_size: 0
   >           where: "size(relations.river) > 0"
   >           attributes:
   >             class: { value: river }
   >             name: "relations.river[0].name"
   >             name_en: "coalesce(relations.river[0]['name:en'], relations.river[0].name)"
   >             name_de: "coalesce(relations.river[0]['name:de'], relations.river[0].name, relations.river[0]['name:en'])"
   >             "name:latin": >-
   >               relations.river[0].name.isLatin() ? relations.river[0].name :
   >               relations.river[0]['name:en'].isLatin() ? relations.river[0]['name:en'] :
   >               relations.river[0].int_name.isLatin() ? relations.river[0].int_name :
   >               relations.river[0]['name:de'].isLatin() ? relations.river[0]['name:de'] : null
   >             "name:nonlatin": "relations.river[0].name.isLatin() ? null : relations.river[0].name.removeLatin()"
   >             name_int: >-
   >               coalesce(relations.river[0].int_name, relations.river[0]['name:en'],
   >               relations.river[0].name.isLatin() ? relations.river[0].name :
   >               relations.river[0]['name:de'].isLatin() ? relations.river[0]['name:de'] : null,
   >               relations.river[0].name)
   >             _relid: { expr: "relations.river[0].id", hidden: true }
   >           merge_lines:
   >             - { minzoom: 6, maxzoom: 8, min_length: 1, tolerance: 0.1, buffer: 4 }
   >             - { minzoom: 9, maxzoom: 9, min_length: 26.17, tolerance: 0.1, buffer: 4 }
   >             - { minzoom: 10, maxzoom: 10, min_length: 26.17, tolerance: 0.1, buffer: 4 }
   >             - { minzoom: 11, maxzoom: 11, min_length: 13.08, tolerance: 0.1, buffer: 4 }
   >         waterway:
   >           geometry: line
   >           buffer: 416
   >           minzoom: 9
   >           maxzoom: 11
   >           simplify: 0.1
   >           min_size: 0
   >           where: "waterway == 'river' && name != null"
   >           attributes: &waterway_attributes
   >             <<: &names
   >               name: name
   >               name_en: "coalesce(feature['name:en'], name)"
   >               name_de: "coalesce(feature['name:de'], name, feature['name:en'])"
   >               "name:latin": &name_latin >-
   >                 name.isLatin() ? name : feature['name:en'].isLatin() ? feature['name:en'] :
   >                 int_name.isLatin() ? int_name : feature['name:de'].isLatin() ? feature['name:de'] :
   >                 [feature['name:af'], feature['name:am'], feature['name:ar'], feature['name:az'],
   >                 feature['name:be'], feature['name:bg'], feature['name:bn'], feature['name:br'],
   >                 feature['name:bs'], feature['name:ca'], feature['name:co'], feature['name:cs'],
   >                 feature['name:cy'], feature['name:da'], feature['name:el'], feature['name:eo'],
   >                 feature['name:es'], feature['name:et'], feature['name:eu'], feature['name:fa'],
   >                 feature['name:fi'], feature['name:fr'], feature['name:fy'], feature['name:ga'],
   >                 feature['name:gd'], feature['name:he'], feature['name:hi'], feature['name:hr'],
   >                 feature['name:hu'], feature['name:hy'], feature['name:id'], feature['name:is'],
   >                 feature['name:it'], feature['name:ja'], feature['name:ja_kana'], feature['name:ja_rm'],
   >                 feature['name:ja-Latn'], feature['name:ja-Hira'], feature['name:ka'],
   >                 feature['name:kk'], feature['name:kn'], feature['name:ko'], feature['name:ko-Latn'],
   >                 feature['name:ku'], feature['name:la'], feature['name:lb'], feature['name:lt'],
   >                 feature['name:lv'], feature['name:mk'], feature['name:mt'], feature['name:ml'],
   >                 feature['name:nl'], feature['name:no'], feature['name:oc'], feature['name:pa'],
   >                 feature['name:pnb'], feature['name:pl'], feature['name:pt'], feature['name:rm'],
   >                 feature['name:ro'], feature['name:ru'], feature['name:sk'], feature['name:sl'],
   >                 feature['name:sq'], feature['name:sr'], feature['name:sr-Latn'], feature['name:sv'],
   >                 feature['name:ta'], feature['name:te'], feature['name:th'], feature['name:tok'],
   >                 feature['name:tr'], feature['name:uk'], feature['name:ur'], feature['name:vi'],
   >                 feature['name:zh'], feature['name:zh-Hant'], feature['name:zh-Hans']].filter(n,
   >                 n.isLatin()).min()
   >               "name:nonlatin": "name.isLatin() ? null : name.removeLatin()"
   >               name_int: &name_int >-
   >                 coalesce(int_name, feature['name:en'], (name.isLatin() ? name :
   >                 feature['name:en'].isLatin() ? feature['name:en'] : int_name.isLatin() ? int_name :
   >                 feature['name:de'].isLatin() ? feature['name:de'] : [feature['name:af'],
   >                 feature['name:am'], feature['name:ar'], feature['name:az'], feature['name:be'],
   >                 feature['name:bg'], feature['name:bn'], feature['name:br'], feature['name:bs'],
   >                 feature['name:ca'], feature['name:co'], feature['name:cs'], feature['name:cy'],
   >                 feature['name:da'], feature['name:el'], feature['name:eo'], feature['name:es'],
   >                 feature['name:et'], feature['name:eu'], feature['name:fa'], feature['name:fi'],
   >                 feature['name:fr'], feature['name:fy'], feature['name:ga'], feature['name:gd'],
   >                 feature['name:he'], feature['name:hi'], feature['name:hr'], feature['name:hu'],
   >                 feature['name:hy'], feature['name:id'], feature['name:is'], feature['name:it'],
   >                 feature['name:ja'], feature['name:ja_kana'], feature['name:ja_rm'],
   >                 feature['name:ja-Latn'], feature['name:ja-Hira'], feature['name:ka'],
   >                 feature['name:kk'], feature['name:kn'], feature['name:ko'], feature['name:ko-Latn'],
   >                 feature['name:ku'], feature['name:la'], feature['name:lb'], feature['name:lt'],
   >                 feature['name:lv'], feature['name:mk'], feature['name:mt'], feature['name:ml'],
   >                 feature['name:nl'], feature['name:no'], feature['name:oc'], feature['name:pa'],
   >                 feature['name:pnb'], feature['name:pl'], feature['name:pt'], feature['name:rm'],
   >                 feature['name:ro'], feature['name:ru'], feature['name:sk'], feature['name:sl'],
   >                 feature['name:sq'], feature['name:sr'], feature['name:sr-Latn'], feature['name:sv'],
   >                 feature['name:ta'], feature['name:te'], feature['name:th'], feature['name:tok'],
   >                 feature['name:tr'], feature['name:uk'], feature['name:ur'], feature['name:vi'],
   >                 feature['name:zh'], feature['name:zh-Hant'], feature['name:zh-Hans']].filter(n,
   >                 n.isLatin()).min()), name)
   >               "name:*": "name:*"
   >             class: waterway
   >             brunnel:
   >               expr: >-
   >                 bridge != null && !(bridge in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 'bridge' : tunnel != null &&
   >                 !(tunnel in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 'tunnel' : null
   >               minzoom: 12
   >             intermittent:
   >               expr: "intermittent != null && !(intermittent in ['0', 'false', 'no']) ? 1 : 0"
   >               minzoom: 12
   >         waterway_z12:
   >           layer: waterway
   >           geometry: line
   >           buffer: 64
   >           min_size_at_maxzoom: 0.0625
   >           minzoom: "waterway in ['river', 'canal'] ? 12 : 13"
   >           where: "waterway in ['stream', 'river', 'canal', 'drain', 'ditch']"
   >           attributes: *waterway_attributes
   >         # landcover: OSM only, from z7; the zoom bands stand in for Planetiler's minimum size per zoom
   >         landcover:
   >           geometry: polygon
   >           buffer: 64
   >           minzoom: 7
   >           maxzoom: 9
   >           simplify: 0.25
   >           min_size: 2
   >           where: &landcover_where >-
   >             landuse in ['allotments', 'farm', 'farmland', 'orchard', 'flowerbed', 'plant_nursery',
   >             'vineyard', 'grass', 'grassland', 'meadow', 'forest', 'village_green', 'recreation_ground'] ||
   >             natural in ['wood', 'wetland', 'fell', 'grassland', 'heath', 'scrub', 'shrubbery', 'tundra',
   >             'glacier', 'bare_rock', 'scree', 'beach', 'sand', 'dune'] || leisure in ['park', 'garden',
   >             'golf_course'] || wetland in ['bog', 'swamp', 'wet_meadow', 'marsh', 'reedbed', 'saltern',
   >             'tidalflat', 'saltmarsh', 'mangrove']
   >           attributes: &landcover_attributes
   >             class: >-
   >               {'farmland': 'farmland', 'farm': 'farmland', 'orchard': 'farmland', 'vineyard': 'farmland',
   >               'plant_nursery': 'farmland', 'glacier': 'ice', 'wood': 'wood', 'forest': 'wood',
   >               'bare_rock': 'rock', 'scree': 'rock', 'fell': 'grass', 'flowerbed': 'grass', 'grassland':
   >               'grass', 'heath': 'grass', 'scrub': 'grass', 'shrubbery': 'grass', 'tundra': 'grass',
   >               'grass': 'grass', 'meadow': 'grass', 'allotments': 'grass', 'park': 'grass',
   >               'village_green': 'grass', 'recreation_ground': 'grass', 'garden': 'grass', 'golf_course':
   >               'grass', 'wetland': 'wetland', 'bog': 'wetland', 'swamp': 'wetland', 'wet_meadow':

   >                 'disc_golf', 'diving', 'dog_racing', 'equestrian', 'fatsal', 'field_hockey',
   >                 'free_flying', 'gaelic_games', 'golf', 'gymnastics', 'handball', 'hockey',
   >                 'horse_racing', 'horseshoes', 'ice_hockey', 'ice_stock', 'judo', 'karting', 'korfball',
   >                 'long_jump', 'model_aerodrome', 'motocross', 'motor', 'multi', 'netball',
   >                 'orienteering', 'paddle_tennis', 'paintball', 'paragliding', 'pelota', 'racquet',
   >                 'rc_car', 'rowing', 'rugby', 'rugby_league', 'rugby_union', 'running', 'sailing',
   >                 'scuba_diving', 'shooting', 'shooting_range', 'skateboard', 'skating', 'skiing',
   >                 'soccer', 'surfing', 'swimming', 'table_soccer', 'table_tennis', 'team_handball',
   >                 'tennis', 'toboggan', 'volleyball', 'water_ski', 'yoga']
   >               attributes:
   >                 class: >-
   >                   sport in ['american_football', 'soccer'] ? 'stadium' : sport
   >                 subclass: >-
   >                   sport
   >             - where: >-
   >                 zoo in ['enclosure', 'petting_zoo', 'aviary', 'wildlife_park', 'birds', 'safari_park',
   >                 'butterfly', 'falconry', 'reptile', 'terrarium']
   >               attributes:
   >                 class: >-
   >                   zoo == 'enclosure' ? 'enclosure' : 'zoo'
   >                 subclass: >-
   >                   zoo
   >             - where: >-
   >                 tourism in ['alpine_hut', 'aquarium', 'artwork', 'attraction', 'bed_and_breakfast',
   >                 'camp_site', 'caravan_site', 'chalet', 'gallery', 'guest_house', 'hostel', 'hotel',
   >                 'information', 'motel', 'museum', 'picnic_site', 'theme_park', 'viewpoint', 'zoo']
   >               attributes:
   >                 class: >-
   >                   tourism in ['alpine_hut', 'bed_and_breakfast', 'chalet', 'guest_house', 'hostel',
   >                   'hotel', 'motel'] ? 'lodging' : tourism in ['artwork', 'gallery'] ? 'art_gallery' :
   >                   tourism in ['camp_site', 'caravan_site'] ? 'campsite' : tourism == 'viewpoint' ?
   >                   'attraction' : tourism
   >                 subclass: >-
   >                   tourism == 'information' ? information : tourism
   >             - where: >-
   >                 waterway == 'dock'
   >               attributes:
   >                 class: { value: harbor }
   >                 subclass: >-
   >                   waterway
   >           sort_by:
   >             - >-
   >               (amenity in ['hospital', 'nursing_home', 'clinic'] ? 20 : railway in ['station', 'halt',
   >               'tram_stop'] ? 40 : amenity == 'bus_station' || highway == 'bus_stop' ? 50 : tourism in
   >               ['attraction', 'viewpoint'] ? 70 : leisure == 'marina' || waterway == 'dock' ? 75 : amenity
   >               in ['university', 'college'] ? 80 : amenity in ['school', 'kindergarten'] ? 85 : leisure ==
   >               'stadium' || sport in ['american_football', 'soccer'] ? 90 : tourism == 'zoo' || zoo != null
   >               ? 95 : amenity in ['townhall', 'public_building', 'courthouse', 'community_centre'] ? 100 :
   >               tourism in ['camp_site', 'caravan_site'] ? 110 : amenity == 'grave_yard' || landuse ==
   >               'cemetery' ? 115 : leisure == 'park' || amenity == 'bbq' ? 120 : amenity == 'library' ||
   >               shop == 'books' ? 130 : amenity == 'police' ? 135 : amenity in ['post_box', 'post_office',
   >               'parcel_locker'] ? 140 : leisure in ['golf_course', 'miniature_golf'] ? 150 : shop in
   >               ['deli', 'delicatessen', 'department_store', 'greengrocer', 'supermarket'] || amenity ==
   >               'marketplace' ? 500 : amenity in ['fast_food', 'food_court'] ? 600 : shop in ['bag',
   >               'clothes'] ? 700 : amenity in ['bar', 'nightclub'] ? 800 : shop in ['accessories',
   >               'antiques', 'beauty', 'bed', 'boutique', 'camera', 'carpet', 'charity', 'chemist',
   >               'chocolate', 'coffee', 'computer', 'confectionery', 'convenience', 'copyshop', 'cosmetics',
   >               'doityourself', 'electronics', 'erotic', 'fabric', 'florist', 'frozen_food', 'furniture',
   >               'garden_centre', 'general', 'gift', 'hardware', 'hearing_aids', 'hifi',
   >               'interior_decoration', 'jewelry', 'kiosk', 'lamps', 'locksmith', 'mall', 'massage',
   >               'mobile_phone', 'motorcycle', 'newsagent', 'optician', 'outdoor', 'paint', 'perfume',
   >               'perfumery', 'pet', 'photo', 'second_hand', 'shoes', 'sports', 'stationery', 'tailor',
   >               'tattoo', 'ticket', 'tobacco', 'toys', 'travel_agency', 'video', 'video_games', 'watches',
   >               'weapons', 'wholesale'] ? 400 : 1000) + (name == null ? 2000 : 0)
   >           thinning: { method: grid, size: 64, rank: rank }
   >         # aerodrome_label
   >         aerodrome_label:
   >           geometry: [point, polygon_centroid]
   >           buffer: 1024
   >           where: "aeroway == 'aerodrome'"
   >           minzoom: >-
   >             iata != null && (aerodrome == 'international' || aerodrome_type == 'international' ?
   >             'international' : aerodrome == 'public' || aerodrome_type != null &&
   >             aerodrome_type.contains('public') || aerodrome_type == 'civil' ? 'public' : aerodrome ==
   >             'regional' || aerodrome_type == 'regional' ? 'regional' : aerodrome == 'military' ||
   >             aerodrome_type != null && aerodrome_type.contains('military') || military == 'airfield' ?
   >             'military' : aerodrome == 'private' || aerodrome_type == 'private' ? 'private' : 'other') ==
   >             'international' ? 8 : 10
   >           attributes:
   >             <<: *names
   >             ele: *ele
   >             ele_ft: *ele_ft
   >             iata: iata
   >             icao: icao
   >             class: >-
   >               aerodrome == 'international' || aerodrome_type == 'international' ? 'international' :
   >               aerodrome == 'public' || aerodrome_type != null && aerodrome_type.contains('public') ||
   >               aerodrome_type == 'civil' ? 'public' : aerodrome == 'regional' || aerodrome_type ==
   >               'regional' ? 'regional' : aerodrome == 'military' || aerodrome_type != null &&
   >               aerodrome_type.contains('military') || military == 'airfield' ? 'military' : aerodrome ==
   >               'private' || aerodrome_type == 'private' ? 'private' : 'other'
   > ```
3. Generate the tileset of the extract's area. The ocean polygons cover the whole world, so without `--bbox` the tileset does too:

   ```bash
   martin cp --mode bulk --config openmaptiles.yaml --output-file berlin.mbtiles --format mvt --max-zoom 14 \
     --bbox 13.08,52.33,13.77,52.68
   ```
4. Serve it, and point the `openmaptiles` source of a style at `http://localhost:3000/berlin`:

   ```bash
   martin berlin.mbtiles
   ```

A Berlin run, next to Planetiler on the same extract:

| Run | PBF | Features | Tiles | Size | Time | Memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Martin, Berlin, 2026-11-11 | 100 MB | 1,724,829 | 912 | 45.4 MB | 1m 8s | 8.4 GB |
| Planetiler 0.10.2, the same extract | 100 MB | \- | 942 | 41.8 MB | 1m 19s | 5.0 GB |

Measured on 24 threads, with the extract and the ocean polygons in the page cache. Martin unpacks the ocean polygons in 6 s and keeps whole tiles of the `--bbox`. Planetiler's time includes 23 s of Natural Earth and lake centerline downloads and 15 s reading the ocean polygons, and it covers the extract's own bounds.

## How closely it matches Planetiler

Martin's tests render the inputs of Planetiler's OpenMapTiles layer tests, and 231 of its 341 examples match. The other 110 come from the differences in [How it differs](<#how-it-differs-from-planetilers-openmaptiles>), or from tests that check something other than the rendered tile:

| Examples | Why they do not match |
| ---: | --- |
| 33 | Natural Earth and lake centerline inputs, which are not read |
| 16 | Country borders with `adm0_l`/`adm0_r`, which Planetiler draws after reading the file, outside the tested code |
| 16 | Natural Earth ranks of countries, states, cities and seas |
| 11 | `rank` from the label grid, which Planetiler's tests leave out and Martin's tiles have |
| 8 | GB and IE road networks |
| 5 | Feature lengths: short trunks at z5, `brunnel` by size |
| 5 | Ocean polygons and large lakes below z6, and inputs the tests' whole-world polygons were shrunk to 1° for |
| 4 | `route_N` order and duplicates |
| 4 | Wikidata translations, translated names of river relations |
| 4 | `--boundary-osm-only` zooms, `hide_3d`, `customary_ft` |
| 3 | A minimum size dropping a feature below the zoom Planetiler declares, an attribute asked below the feature's zoom |
| 1 | A closed `man_made=pier` way drawn as a line too |

## How it differs from Planetiler's OpenMapTiles

The configuration reads OpenStreetMap and the ocean polygons only. Planetiler also reads Natural Earth, the lake centerlines and Wikidata, and runs code that `martin cp` has no equivalent for yet:

| Layer | Planetiler | This configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all | Wikidata translations and transliterated `name:latin` | Only the `name:xx` tags of the 81 OpenMapTiles languages |
| `water` | Natural Earth ocean and lakes at z0-5, ocean polygons from z6 | Ocean polygons from z0; OpenStreetMap lakes of 25 km² and more at z4-5 (2000 km² from z2, 20000 km² from z0) |
| `water` | A Natural Earth lake's `id` is the OpenStreetMap lake it overlaps most | Large lakes keep their own `id` at z0-5 |
| `waterway` | Natural Earth rivers at z3-5; river relation members at z6-8 only when the whole river is long enough | No rivers below z6; at z6-8 every member of a named `waterway=river` relation, merged and kept from 1 px |
| `waterway` | Relation names in all languages, members with role `main_stream` or none | Relation `name`, `name_en`, `name_de`, `name:latin`, `name:nonlatin`, `name_int`; any role |
| `landcover` | Natural Earth glaciers and ice shelves at z0-6 | From z7 only |
| `landcover` | Merges wood and forest of fewer than 300 vertices at z8-13 | Merges all wood and forest at z8-13, as there is no vertex count |
| `landuse` | Natural Earth urban areas at z4-5 | From z6 only |
| `mountain_peak` | `customary_ft` inside the United States; no `rank` at z14 beyond the grid | No `customary_ft`; `rank` from the z0-13 grid only |
| `boundary` | Natural Earth lines at z0-4, OpenStreetMap from z4-5 | OpenStreetMap from z0, as Planetiler's `--boundary-osm-only` |
| `boundary` | `adm0_l` and `adm0_r` from the country polygons left and right of each border | No `adm0_l` and `adm0_r` |
| `boundary` | Borders joined across ways by a line merger before tiling | Joined per tile by `merge_lines` |
| `place` | Country, state and city ranks from Natural Earth polygons and points nearby | Country ranks from Natural Earth by ISO code (`openmaptiles_ranks.py`), every state and province with rank 6, city ranks from `population` and `capital` |
| `transportation` | `network` and z4-5 roads from GB and IE `ref` patterns inside Natural Earth country polygons | US and Canadian networks from route relations only |
| `transportation` | Trunk segments shorter than 500 m at z5, as `motorway` up to z5 | Trunk from z6 unless a route relation upgrades it |
| `transportation` | `brunnel` and `layer` from z4 and z9 on segments longer than 4 px | `brunnel` and `layer` from z12 |
| `transportation` | Closed `man_made=pier` ways are only polygons | Also drawn as `pier` lines |
| `transportation_name` | `route_N` sorted by network type, network and `ref`, without duplicates | `route_1` to `route_6` in relation id order, duplicates kept |
| `transportation_name` | `motorway_junction` class from the highest road through the node | `class` is always `motorway` |
| `transportation_name` | z12-13 lines shorter than 6 px per letter of the name are dropped | z12-13 merged lines shorter than 60 px, a name of 10 letters, are dropped |
| `building` | `hide_3d` from `type=building` relations | No `hide_3d` |
| `water_name` | Lake centerlines as labels; Natural Earth ranks of seas | Points only; sea ranks from the `rank` tag |
| `poi` | `agg_stop` picks one stop of each group sharing a `uic_ref` | No `agg_stop` |
| point layers | `buffer` of 256 px | 127.9 px, the most an `extent` of 4096 allows |
| point layers | Points from polygons dropped while the polygon is below a minimum size (university, lake label) | The same as a `minzoom` from the polygon's area |
| `poi`, `place` | Draw order by class rank and Natural Earth rank | Class rank from the tags, without telling apart keys of one object |
| `building` | Heights in any unit Planetiler parses | Meters, kilometers, feet and inches, miles and nautical miles |
| all | `min_size` compares the square root of a polygon's area and a line's length | Compares the larger side of the bounding box, so more thin polygons and lines stay |
| `landuse` | Residential areas closer than 0.2 px joined at z9-12 | Closer than 0.1 px, as larger distances could not make a valid union in Berlin |

## Changing the configuration

The configuration uses three patterns that you need to know before you change it.

**Zoom bands.** Martin clamps a `minzoom` or `maxzoom` to its layer's zooms. Where Planetiler changes a feature's settings by zoom, the configuration splits the layer into one layer per zoom band. Each band has its own `min_size` and `buffer`, and all bands write into one output layer with [`layer`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#combining-layers>).

**Conditions as zooms.** A `where` that the PBF reader cannot check, such as one calling `area()` or a regular expression, makes Martin read every object in the file. The configuration puts such conditions into `minzoom` and `maxzoom` expressions instead. Martin leaves out a feature whose `minzoom` ends up above its `maxzoom`. In `water_lakes_low`, which draws large lakes up to z5, a lake below 25 km^2 gets a `minzoom` of 5 and a `maxzoom` of 0, so that layer leaves it out.

**Selective merges.** Planetiler merges only some features of a layer, such as only wood and forest in `landcover`. The configuration gives every other feature a [hidden attribute](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#hidden-attributes>) `_unmerged` set to its feature id, `osm_id * 10` plus 2 for a way or 3 for a relation. A way and a relation can share an `osm_id`, but no two features share a feature id, so they never merge.

# PostgreSQL SSL Certificates

Martin supports SSL certificate authentication for PostgreSQL connections. This guide covers certificate generation, PostgreSQL configuration, and Martin setup.

## When to Use SSL Certificates

Use SSL certificates for:

- Deployments where Martin and PostGIS are on separate machines
- Compliance requirements (PCI DSS, HIPAA, etc.)
- Cloud PostgreSQL deployments
- High-security environments requiring certificate-based authentication

## SSL Modes

There are not many cases where anything between the two recommended modes makes sense. In particular, the default mode (`prefer`) does not make much sense. From the postgres documentation:

> As is shown in the table, this makes no sense from a security point of view, and it only promises performance overhead if possible. It is only provided as the default for backward compatibility, and is not recommended in secure deployments.

For a fuller explanation of the different tradeoffs, refer to the [PostgreSQL SSL Certificates documentation](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-ssl.html#LIBPQ-SSL-CONFIG>).

## Generating Certificates

For basic SSL encryption, you need:

- `server-cert.pem` - PostgreSQL server certificate
- `server-key.pem` - PostgreSQL server private key
- `ca-cert.pem` - Certificate Authority certificate

```text
┌─────────────────┐    SSL/TLS     ┌─────────────────┐
│     Martin      │◄─────────────►│   PostgreSQL    │
└─────────────────┘   verify-full  └─────────────────┘
         │                                   │
    ┌─────────┐                        ┌─────────────┐
    │ CA Cert │                        │ Server Cert │
    │         │                        │ Server Key  │
    └─────────┘                        └─────────────┘
```

### Self-Signed Certificates

To generate certificates as a CA, you will need a private key. To verify the certificate, you will need the CA certificate.

```bash
# Generate CA private key
openssl genrsa -out ca-key.pem 3072

# Generate CA certificate
openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -key ca-key.pem -out ca-cert.pem \
    -subj "/C=US/ST=State/L=City/O=Organization/CN=Test CA"
```

You can then generate a server certificate:

```bash
# Generate server private key
openssl genrsa -out server-key.pem 3072

# Generate server certificate signing request with SAN extension
openssl req -new -key server-key.pem -out server-csr.pem \
    -subj "/C=US/ST=State/L=City/O=Organization/CN=localhost" \
    -addext "subjectAltName = DNS:localhost"

# Generate server certificate signed by CA with SAN extension
openssl x509 -req -days 365 -in server-csr.pem \
    -CA ca-cert.pem -CAkey ca-key.pem \
    -CAcreateserial -out server-cert.pem -extensions v3_req \
    -extfile <(printf "[v3_req]\nsubjectAltName = DNS:localhost")

# Set permissions
chmod 400 *-key.pem
chmod 444 *-cert.pem ca-cert.pem
```

### Production Certificates

For production, use certificates from:

- Regular Certificate Authorities (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, GlobalSign)
- Cloud provider managed Certificate Authorities
- Organization-Internal Certificate Authority

## PostgreSQL Configuration

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgis/postgis:17-3.5
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - ./server-cert.pem:/var/lib/postgresql/server.crt:ro
      - ./server-key.pem:/var/lib/postgresql/server.key:ro
    command:
      - -c
      - ssl=on
      - -c
      - ssl_cert_file=/var/lib/postgresql/server.crt
      - -c
      - ssl_key_file=/var/lib/postgresql/server.key
```

```bash
docker compose up
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Postgres requires specific file permissions and ownership for SSL certificates. In docker this can be a bit tricky:
>
> alpine images have `70:70` as the default `user:group` debian images have `999:999` as the default `user:group`
>
> You can change this by running the following commands:
>
> ```bash
> chown 999:999 *.pem
> chmod 400 *.pem
> ```

## Testing with psql

Test SSL Connection via

```bash
export PGSSLROOTCERT=ca-cert.pem
psql "postgres://postgres:password@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=verify-full"
```

> [!TIP]
>
> If you get file permission errors, make sure the current user can access the files. The previous step may set them to not readable by the current user.

Then, verify SSL Status by

```sql
-- Enable SSL info extension (required for ssl_is_used function)
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS sslinfo;

-- Check SSL status
SELECT ssl_is_used();

-- SSL connection details
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid();
```

## Martin Configuration

Martin can be configured using [the CLI](<https://maplibre.org/martin/run-with-cli/index.md>) or the [configuration file](<https://maplibre.org/martin/config-file/index.md>). Which of them you choose is up to you. You do not need to configure things twice.

**Configuration File (click to expand)**

```yaml
postgres:
  ssl_root_cert: './ca-cert.pem'
  connection_string: 'postgres://postgres:password@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=verify-full'
```

**Command Line (click to expand)**

```bash
martin --ca-root-file ./ca-cert.pem \
      "postgres://postgres:password@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=verify-full"
```

## Troubleshooting

You can get more context via the following commands:

```bash
export PGSSLMODE=verify-full
export PGSSLROOTCERT=./ca-cert.pem
# Verbose psql
psql -h localhost -U postgres -d postgres -v

# Debug Martin
RUST_LOG=debug RUST_LOG_FORMAT=pretty martin --ca-root-file ./ca-cert.pem postgres://...
```

These are the errors that can occur:

**Certificate verification failed (click to expand)**

- Check server certificate is signed by the CA
- Verify the CA certificate path given as `--ca-root-file` or `ssl_root_cert`
- Ensure certificate files are readable

**Hostname verification failed (click to expand)**

- Server certificate CN/SAN must match hostname
- Use `verify-ca` instead of `verify-full` if hostname doesn't match

**Permission denied (click to expand)**

- Check certificate file permissions
- Private keys should be `chmod 400` and readable by the user running the application

**Connection refused (click to expand)**

- Verify PostgreSQL accepts SSL connections
- Check `pg_hba.conf` allows SSL from your IP

## Security Best Practices if using postgres via SSL

- Use at least 3072-bit RSA keys
- Protect private keys with restricted permissions (`chmod 400`)
- Rotate certificates before expiration
- Use `verify-full` in production
- Monitor certificate expiration
- Store `ca-key.pem` securely (only needed for certificate management)
- Use secure secret management for production certificates

# Tools

# Generating Tiles in Bulk

Martin offers the `martin cp` subcommand for generating tiles in bulk, from any source(s) supported by Martin, and save retrieved tiles into a new or an existing MBTiles file.

`martin cp` can be used to generate tiles for a large area or multiple areas (bounding boxes). If multiple areas overlap, it will ensure each tile is generated only once `martin cp` supports the same configuration file and CLI arguments as the Martin server, so it can support all sources and even combining sources.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Generating tiles from features**
>
> By default, `martin cp` asks the source for each tile, so the source must contain or generate the tiles. `martin cp` can also [generate tiles from features](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/index.md>): it reads each source's features once and builds the whole tileset inside Martin, using a method adapted from [Planetiler](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler>).

The released `martin` binary does not include [DuckDB / GeoParquet sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-duckdb/index.md>). To use them, build `martin` with the feature and list the source in the configuration file:

```bash
cargo build --package martin --bin martin --features=unstable-duckdb
```

After copying, `martin cp` will update the `agg_tiles_hash` metadata value unless `--skip-agg-tiles-hash` is specified. This allows the MBTiles file to be [validated](<https://maplibre.org/martin/mbtiles-validation/index.md#aggregate-content-validation>) using `mbtiles validate` command.

`--set-meta KEY=VALUE` and `--delete-meta KEY` edit the metadata after the copy, so they can override the computed values. A key that is both set and deleted is an error, and nothing is copied.

## Usage

This copies tiles from a PostGIS table `my_table` into an MBTiles file `tileset.mbtiles` using [normalized](<https://maplibre.org/martin/mbtiles-schema/index.md#normalized>) schema, with zoom levels from 0 to 10, and xyz-compliant tile bounds of the whole world.

```bash
martin cp  --output-file tileset.mbtiles                         \
           --mbtiles-type normalized                             \
           "--bbox=-180,-85.05112877980659,180,85.0511287798066" \
           --min-zoom 0                                          \
           --max-zoom 10                                         \
           --source source_name                                  \
           postgres://postgres@localhost:5432/db
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Next to regular sources, `--source <SOURCE>` does support [composite sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-composite/index.md>). This means `martin cp` can be used to merge two different sources into one `mbtiles` archive.

If performance is a concern, you should also consider

> [!TIP]
>
> `--concurrency <CONCURRENCY>` and `--pool-size <POOL_SIZE>` can be used to control the number of concurrent requests and the pool size for postgres sources respectively.
>
> The optimal setting depends on:
>
> - the source(s) performance characteristics
> - how much load is allowed, for example in a multi-tenant environment
> - how to compress tiles stored in the output file

You should also consider

> [!TIP]
>
> `--encoding <ENCODING>` can be used to reduce the final size of the MBTiles file or decrease the amount of processing `martin cp` does.
>
> The default `gzip` should be a reasonable choice for most use cases, but if you prefer a different encoding, you can specify it here. If set to multiple values like `'gzip,br'`, `martin cp` will use the first encoding, or re-encode if the tile is already encoded and that encoding is not listed. Use `identity` to disable compression. Ignored for non-encodable tiles like PNG and JPEG.

> [!NOTE]
>
> When the source (such as PG tables) guarantees that an empty tile only has empty tiles below it, `martin cp` copies zoom by zoom and never fetches the tiles below an empty tile. This means that even sparse sources can usually be fairly performant.

## Modes

`--mode` chooses how `martin cp` produces the tiles:

- `tile` requests every tile from the source, as the tile server does.
- `bulk` reads each table once and renders every zoom itself, which is much faster for whole tilesets. See [Generating Tilesets](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/index.md>).
- `auto` is the default. It picks `tile` for now, and will pick `bulk` for every run it can handle.

Each mode refuses the options only the other one reads.

## MLT from PostgreSQL tables

With `--format mlt`, `martin cp` encodes a PostgreSQL table source's tiles straight from its rows instead of converting the MVT tile PostGIS builds. The tiles describe the same features as that conversion would:

- A column type a tile property cannot hold, such as an array, a `numeric` or a timestamp, is written as its text, as `ST_AsMVT` writes it.
- A `jsonb` column is spread over one property per top-level key that holds a string, a boolean or a number, as `ST_AsMVT` spreads it. Nested objects, arrays and `null`s are left out.

Function sources, and tiles the row query cannot encode, go through the MVT conversion instead, and `martin cp` logs a warning when that happens.

A `martin` built with the `unstable-mlt-v2` feature also accepts `--format mlt2`, which keeps what the v1 wire format has no place for:

- A `jsonb` document is kept whole, nested values included, in a nested column named after the `jsonb` column.
- The M ordinates of measured geometries are kept in a vertex column named `m`. PostGIS drops the M ordinates of every geometry it clips at the tile border, so with the default `clip_geom: true` only the features that lie wholly inside the tile and its buffer keep them. Set `clip_geom: false` on the table to keep them everywhere.

## Arguments

Use `martin cp --help` to see a list of available options:

```text
Bulk copy tiles from any Martin-supported sources into an mbtiles file

Usage: martin cp [OPTIONS] --output-file <OUTPUT_FILE> [CONNECTION]...

Arguments:
  [CONNECTION]...
```
