```
        Bounds["auto_bounds<br/>ST_Extent_Approx / ST_Extent"]
    end

    subgraph Request["Per tile request"]
        XYZ["z / x / y"]
        SQL["ST_Transform + ST_AsMVTGeom"]
        MVT["ST_AsMVT"]
    end

    File --> Pool --> Describe --> CRS --> Bounds
    Pool -.->|pooled connection| SQL
    XYZ --> SQL --> MVT
```

**GeoParquet load time** (`DuckDBSource`):

1. Martin creates a DuckDB connection pool. Local GeoParquet uses an in-memory database with the `spatial` extension; remote `http(s)` URLs also load `httpfs`.
2. Columns are discovered with `DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM read_parquet(...)`. The geometry column is taken from config, or auto-detected when there is exactly one geometry column.
3. SRID is taken from config, or from `ST_CRS` on the first non-null geometry (EPSG and `OGC:CRS84` only).
4. TileJSON bounds are computed according to `auto_bounds` (`quick`, `calc`, or `skip`).
5. An MVT SQL query is built once and executed per tile with `z`, `x`, `y` parameters.

**GeoParquet requests** (`DuckDBSource::get_tile`):

1. A connection is taken from the pool and the tile query runs on a blocking thread.
2. Geometry is stamped with the source CRS, transformed to Web Mercator (`EPSG:3857`), filtered to the tile envelope (expanded by `buffer`), clipped with `ST_AsMVTGeom`, and encoded with `ST_AsMVT`.
3. Non-geometry columns become MVT feature properties. `id_column`, if set, becomes the MVT feature id.
4. The tile is returned uncompressed as `application/x-protobuf`; the shared server layer then handles caching, ETag/`304`, and `Content-Encoding`, identically to every other source.

**Database files** are opened read-only. Each `database` entry creates one connection pool shared by its table and macro sources. Geometry tables use the same MVT generation path as GeoParquet; `(z, x, y)` table macros return ready-made tiles.

**Configuration** (`DuckDbConfig`; requires `--features=unstable-duckdb`):

`martin data.parquet` and `martin tiles.duckdb` use the default settings. The database command publishes geometry tables and `(z, x, y)` tile macros. Use a [configuration file](<https://maplibre.org/martin/config-file/index.md>) for remote GeoParquet or custom settings:

- `pool_size` (default `4`) - connection pool size per GeoParquet source or database entry.
- `auto_bounds` (default `quick`) - how TileJSON bounds are computed.
- Per-source `geoparquet` path or URL, plus optional `layer_id`, `geometry_column`, `srid`, `extent`, `buffer`, and `clip_geom`.
- `database` file path, with optional `auto_publish`, `tables`, and `macros` to control which sources are published. See [DuckDB database sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-duckdb/index.md#database-sources>).

DuckDB sources do not currently hot-reload.

## Reloading sources

After startup, Martin keeps the catalog in sync with its sources without a restart. One generic loop - the **Reload Driver** - sits behind three traits, so every source kind reuses the same loop and only the kind-specific parts vary.

```
graph LR
    Trigger["Trigger<br/>(when)"] -->|fires| Driver[Reload Driver]
    Driver -->|discover| Discovery["Discovery<br/>(what should exist)"]
    Discovery -->|"(Version, Args) per id"| Driver
    Driver -->|"diff vs baseline, build changed"| Advisory["ReloadAdvisory<br/>add / update / remove"]
    Advisory -->|apply| Sink["Sink<br/>(where)"]
    Sink --> Catalog[("Catalog<br/>TileSourceManager")]
```

The traits are:

- **`Discovery`** - the cheap **"what should exist now"** read (a directory scan or object-store listing). Returns one `(Version, Args)` per source id. `Version` is a `u128` change token (e.g. mtime millis); a changed value triggers an in-place update. `Args` is the kind-specific payload used to build the source on demand.
- **`Trigger`** - decides **when to reconcile**. `NotifyTrigger` fires on filesystem events; `PollTrigger` fires on a fixed interval.
- **`Sink`** - where the diff is **applied**. `TileSourceManager`, which holds the live catalog, implements it directly via `apply_changes`.

They interact in this loop:

1. **Init or seed**. PostgreSQL drivers `init()`: run Discovery once, apply everything, record it as the baseline before serving. `fs` sources loaded during configuration resolution, so their drivers only seed (record a baseline, apply nothing).
2. **Reconcile**. On each Trigger, re-run Discovery. Diff the new `Version`s against the baseline into a `ReloadAdvisory`. Build only the changed ids. Apply through the Sink.
3. **Commit / retain**. Advance the baseline only on a successful apply. A failed discovery or apply keeps the old baseline so the next Trigger retries the same delta, and the catalog never flaps.

Each kind has at least one Reload Driver instance. Adding reload support for a new kind means writing one `Discovery` adapter. The loop, triggers, and sink are reused.

# Generation Architecture

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Not fully implemented**
>
> The bulk mode of `martin cp` is in the release binaries since 2.0.0-beta.6, but parts of what these pages describe are not implemented yet, and the configuration of `layers` may still change.
>
> - [x] Rendering points, lines and polygons, with fill ranges for covered tiles
> - [x] Tile grouping, MLT and MVT encoding, compression and deduplication
> - [x] Planning tables into layers and running a whole generation end to end
> - [x] The PostgreSQL source with partitioned whole-table scans
> - [x] Bulk mode in `martin cp`, and PMTiles output
> - [x] Layers with CEL expressions, `rules` and `sort_by`
> - [x] [OSM PBF files](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-osm/index.md>) and [shapefiles](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-shapefile/index.md>) as sources
> - [ ] GeoPackage and CSV files as sources
> - [x] `geometry` with Planetiler's `polygon_centroid`, `line_centroid`, `centroid`, `polygon_point_on_surface` and `polygon_centroid_if_convex`
> - [ ] `geometry` with Planetiler's `line_midpoint`, `point_on_line` and `innermost_point`
> - [x] [Per-tile operations](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#per-tile-operations>) (`merge_lines`, `merge_polygons`, `thinning`, `merge_multi`, `limit`)

The [bulk mode](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/index.md>) of `martin cp` turns whole sources into a tileset in two phases. First, every feature is read once and rendered into tile pieces, which are sorted on disk by tile. Then the sorted pieces are merged back into tiles, encoded, and written in the order the archive stores them. Every step hands its work to the next through a bounded queue, so the whole run needs a fixed amount of memory, whatever the input size.

Martin implements this via two traits:

- a `FeatureSource` streams features from partitions that can be read in parallel, and
- a `TileSink` writes finished tiles in the order it asks for.

Another database or file format is another `FeatureSource`, and another archive format is another `TileSink`.

The tile server renders a table source with `layers` with the same engine, one tile or one block of tiles at a time and in memory, see [Serving tiles](<#serving-tiles>).

## Motivation and Planetiler

A long-requested Martin feature is generating tiles on the fly from a feature source (raw data) inside Martin itself, when serving tiles. Until now, every source had to either already contain tiles (MBTiles, PMTiles) or generate them itself, like PostgreSQL does with `ST_AsMVT`. Martin only passed those tiles along.

Martin adapted the tile generation method of [Planetiler](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler>), written by Mike Barry ([@msbarry](<https://github.com/msbarry>)) and licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler/blob/main/LICENSE>). Thank you, Mike, for an amazing tool, and thanks to the Planetiler contributors. Martin also adapted a similar layer configuration system, which takes features from any source Martin supports that can produce a stream of features (a `FeatureSource`).

As part of this effort, Martin can now generate a whole tileset at once, as Planetiler does. This expands the existing [`martin cp`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-cp/index.md>) command: only its internals change, so that it supports more than one method of copying data from a source to an archive. Besides asking the source for each tile, it can read each source's features once and build the tiles itself. The tile server uses the same engine to render the tiles of a PostgreSQL table source with `layers` as they are requested.

This method follows Planetiler in:

- reading every feature once and rendering it at every zoom, instead of querying the source per tile,
- sorting the rendered pieces on disk by tile, then merging them back and writing each tile once,
- covering the inside of large polygons with [fill ranges](<#rendering>) instead of one piece per tile,
- simplification and minimum size [in pixels of a 256-pixel tile](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#simplification-and-minimum-size>), with the same defaults,
- [encoding tile batches in parallel and writing them in order](<#parallel-encoding-ordered-writing>),
- reusing the previous tile's bytes and hashing only likely duplicates, see [repeated tiles](<#repeated-tiles>),
- storing repeated tiles once, in the same deduplicated MBTiles layout.

## Phase 1: read and render

### Partitions

A `FeatureSource` declares how many partitions it has, and streams one partition when asked. Readers read different partitions at the same time, at most one reader per thread. In return, a source promises two things:

- **Stable order**: every partition is read in the same row order on every run. With the partition numbers, that fixes the order of the features whatever the thread timing, see [the sort key](<#sort-key>). It need not be the order of one scan, so a source can split its data however it reads fastest.
- **Consistent data**: every partition is read from the same state of the data, even if it changes during the run.

How a source splits its data is up to the source. A file can split by byte range or row group, a database by page range or by id.

The PostgreSQL source splits each table by what the relation allows:

| Relation | Partitions |
| --- | --- |
| Tables and materialized views | Page ranges (`ctid >= '(start,0)' AND ctid < '(end,0)'`), 16384 pages each. The last range is open, so rows added since are still read |
| Anything else with an integer `id_column` | 32 partitions by id remainder (`abs(id % 32) = k`). The first also takes `NULL` ids |
| Anything else | One scan |

Partitions are numbered table by table in physical order. For consistent data, one connection exports a snapshot (`pg_export_snapshot()`), and every reader imports it in a `REPEATABLE READ` transaction before reading its first partition. PostgreSQL's own parallel workers and synchronized scans are turned off on these connections, so each partition is read in its own order, at the pace the generator asks for. There is one reader per two render workers, and no more readers than the pool's `pool_size`.

Each scan reads only the rows some layer takes, when the database can apply every layer's `geometry` and `where`, see [Features](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#features>).

### Feature queue

Readers claim the next partition from a shared counter and stream it as batches of up to 1024 features. The batches go into one queue that holds at most `threads × 2` batches, and every render worker takes the next batch from it. When the workers fall behind, the queue fills and the readers wait, which in turn stops reading from the source. Memory does not grow with the source, and fast readers never race ahead of slow rendering.

Because any worker can take any batch, a slow partition or a feature-heavy area never stalls the other workers.

### Rendering

A render worker takes each feature through every layer its source feeds:

1. The layer's filters decide whether the feature belongs to the layer, and its rules which settings apply.
2. The feature is projected to Web Mercator once, then rendered from its highest zoom down. At each zoom a line or polygon is simplified, and dropped once it is smaller than the minimum size, which also ends the lower zooms, since a feature only shrinks with the zoom. Points are rendered at every zoom.
3. The geometry is sliced into the tiles it touches, keeping its own vertices. No new vertices are cut at tile edges. As in tile mode, a tile keeps what lies on the edge of its buffer too, except a clipped line or polygon that only touches it from outside. A polygon ring that leaves a tile is closed by corners just outside the tile's buffer, where renderers clip it away. A feature that keeps clear of every neighbor tile's buffer, as most do at most zooms, skips the slicer entirely. With `clip_geom: false`, every tile a line or polygon reaches gets the whole geometry instead.
4. Each piece is stored as a record. Its vertices are stored as offsets from the previous vertex, which usually fit in one or two bytes.

The tiles a polygon covers entirely become **fill ranges** instead of one record per tile. A fill range is one record that stands for a contiguous run of tile ids in the archive's tile order, which is a column of tiles in MBTiles order or an aligned quadtree cell in Hilbert order. A huge polygon such as an ocean or a country then costs time and space in proportion to its outline, not its area. An unclipped polygon gets no fill ranges: each covered tile stores it whole.

### Sort key

Every record is sorted by a 16-byte key:

Sorting by this key puts the pieces of each tile next to each other, in the order the archive writes its tiles. Inside a tile, it puts the layers in their configured order, and inside a layer, it keeps the features in source order. The `Seq` part is the feature's partition and row, which do not depend on how the partitions were spread over threads. The tiles are therefore the same whatever the number of threads and their timing.

A layer's `sort_by` value is not part of the key. It travels in the record, and the encoder orders each layer's features by it, keeping the `Seq` order of equal values.

Without `sort_by`, a layer keeps source order, which depends on how the source splits its data. The PostgreSQL source splits a view by id remainder, for example, which interleaves its ids:

Only `sort_by` gives a layer an order that does not depend on the partitions.

### External sort

Each render worker owns a sort buffer of `--memory / threads`, at least 16 MiB and at most 4 GiB. Records are appended to the buffer as they are rendered, and an index of 24-byte entries (key, offset, length) is kept beside them. The budget counts the index twice, because the radix sort needs a second copy of it while sorting. When the records and the index reach the budget, the worker spills the buffer:

1. It radix-sorts the index by key, without moving the records. If the records arrived in increasing `Seq`, as with a single reader, sorting by tile and layer is enough, since the radix sort is stable.
2. It writes the records in key order to a new temporary file, a **sorted run**, as key, length and record, repeated.
3. It clears the buffer and goes on rendering.

Runs go round-robin to the `--temp-dir` directories. They are anonymous temporary files, which the operating system removes when the process ends, even when it is killed.

When every worker has spilled its last buffer, phase 1 ends.

## Phase 2: merge, encode and write

### Merge

A loser-tree merge reads up to 4096 runs at once, each straight from its mapped temp file, and streams their records in key order into phase 2. Only the pieces of one feature in one tile can have equal keys. They come from one worker, and keep the order it pushed them in.

With more than 4096 runs, only the excess is merged first: adjacent runs, just enough that merging them in groups of 4096 leaves 4096 runs in all, picked where they hold the fewest bytes. The groups are merged in parallel into new temp files. The other runs are left for the final merge, which is never written to disk. One such pass is enough for up to 16 777 216 runs. Merging only adjacent runs keeps equal keys in the order they were pushed.

### Grouping

The grouper collects the merged records of one tile at a time. A fill range is kept aside while it still covers upcoming tiles, and added to each of them, so a fill range costs one record however many tiles it covers. The grouper hands tiles on in batches of 256. A batch closes early once it holds 16 MiB of records. The few huge tiles of low zooms then go to several encoders.

### Parallel encoding, ordered writing

Encoding is the expensive part of phase 2, so it runs on all threads, but the archive must receive the tiles in order. The ordered pipeline does both, with a bounded number of batches in flight:

- For each batch, the grouper first puts an empty result **slot** into the **order queue**, then hands the batch to the work queue. The order queue holds `threads × 4` slots. When it is full, the grouper waits.
- Encoders take batches from the work queue in any order, finish them in any order, and put each result into its batch's slot.
- The writer takes slots from the order queue in batch order and waits for each slot's result. A result that arrives early waits in its slot until the writer gets to it.

When one batch is slow, for example a dense city at a high zoom, the other encoders go on with later batches until the order queue is full, and then wait. Memory stays bounded however slow one batch is, and the archive still sees every tile in order.

### Repeated tiles

Each encoder assembles the tile's layers from its records, orders each layer's features by `sort_by`, runs the layer's [per-tile operations](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#per-tile-operations>) on them, encodes them as MLT or MVT, and compresses the result. A layer the operations leave empty is left out of the tile. It also avoids work and storage for repeated tiles:

- A tile with the same records as the encoder's previous tile of the same zoom reuses its bytes without encoding. The operations depend only on the records and the zoom, so the bytes are the same. Neighboring tiles in the archive order are often identical, for example the inside of a large polygon.
- A reused tile, and a tile made only of fill records, gets a dedup key from an index shared by all encoders. The index only hands out a key for bytes equal to the first tile with that hash.

The archive stores tiles with the same dedup key once. Other identical tiles are stored separately.

### Tile order

The archive decides the tile order, and the whole pipeline produces tiles in that order, so the writer never sorts or buffers:

| Archive | Tile order | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MBTiles | Zoom, column, then bottom-up TMS row | The primary key of the `tiles` table, so inserts append to its B-tree instead of splitting pages. Always the deduplicated (`normalized`) schema |
| PMTiles | Hilbert tile id | A clustered archive, written as a stream. Tiles with a dedup key share their bytes |

The tileset's metadata, including the zooms, the format and each layer's fields, is only complete after the last tile, so the archive stores it last.

## Serving tiles

The tile server renders a table source with `layers` with the plan, renderer, grouper and encoder of bulk mode, without its queues and temp files. [Serving](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#serving>) covers its configuration. A request renders a **block**: the tile alone, or with `prefetch`, the block of tiles holding it, see [Prefetch](<#prefetch>).

1. **Read**: one query reads every feature whose geometry meets the block grown by the largest `buffer` of the table's layers. When the grown block crosses the antimeridian, the part past it is read as a second envelope, as bulk mode wraps buffers there too. The query returns whole geometries in the order PostgreSQL finds them, and the features are numbered in that order, as one partition. The query keeps only rows some layer at the block's zoom takes, so `max_feature_count` limits how many of those it returns. Only with `max_feature_count`, `order_by` sorts them by `id_column` first, to choose which are kept.
2. **Render**: one render worker, on a blocking thread, renders the features at the block's zoom only, and slices them into its tiles only, never into the other tiles they reach. The minimum size and simplification still follow the layer's zooms, so each tile comes out as bulk mode writes it for the same `maxzoom`.
3. **Sort**: the sort buffer stays in memory. It grows as records arrive instead of reserving its budget, and is never written to a temp file. The merge reads its records back in key order.
4. **Group and encode**: the grouper and encoder of phase 2, in MBTiles order, write an uncompressed MVT tile for each tile of the block. A tile no feature reaches is empty.

The server then converts, compresses and caches each tile, as it does for any other source.

Inside a layer, the features keep the order the query returns them in, so a layer without `sort_by` can draw them in another order than bulk mode, see [Draw order](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#draw-order>).

### Prefetch

With `prefetch: N`, a cache miss renders the N×N block holding the tile, in one query, and caches all of its tiles, empty ones included. Blocks are aligned to multiples of N, so a request for any tile of a block renders that same block, and is a cache hit once it is rendered. A block at the edge of the world only holds the tiles that exist, so `prefetch: 4` at zoom 1 renders the 2×2 tiles of that zoom.

Each tile goes through the same processing as a requested one, and is cached under the key the request would have for it, for the same source and accepted format. Without a tile cache, or at a zoom outside the cache's zooms, a request renders its tile alone, since nothing could keep the others.

## Memory and disk

Every queue and buffer has a bound that does not depend on the size of the input:

| What | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Feature queue | `threads × 2` batches of up to 1024 features |
| Sort buffers | `--memory` in total, records plus index, at least 16 MiB per worker |
| Run file writers | 1 MiB of write buffer for each run being written |
| Merge | Mapped run files, no read buffers, at most 4096 runs per merge |
| Encode window | `threads × 4` batches of 256 tiles or 16 MiB, plus the one being written |
| Dedup index | One copy of each distinct tile that got a dedup key |

An intermediate merge, with more than 4096 runs, runs several merges at once. On disk, a feature has a record in every tile it touches, at every zoom, and an intermediate merge needs room for another copy of the runs it merges, which are the fewest bytes it can merge.

[Serving a block](<#serving-tiles>) has no such bound and uses no disk: it holds every feature reaching the block, and their records, in memory until its tiles are encoded. A larger `prefetch` holds more.

## Errors

- In phase 1, an error stops every reader from claiming another partition and every worker from taking another batch. The run reports that error, not the hand-offs it interrupted.
- In phase 2, an error of the grouper or an encoder travels to the writer in batch order, as an error in place of a batch. The archive stops there and never finishes a partial tileset. When the writer fails, the grouper's next hand-off fails, and the writer's error is reported.
- Expressions never fail a run, see [Expressions](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/index.md#expressions>). Features the slicer cannot handle at a zoom are skipped at that zoom and counted.
- A failed or interrupted (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>) run removes the output file. The sorted runs are removed by the operating system in every case.
- A served block logs the features the slicer could not handle as warnings. Expression failures are only logged at debug level there, since the plan already warns about the first failure of each expression. A failed query or encoding fails the request.

# Optional

# Migration Guide

Use this guide to update an existing Martin setup after a major release. See the [changelog](<https://maplibre.org/martin/changelog/index.md>) for other changes.

## From 1.x to 2.0

Martin 2.0 removes deprecated options and changes several defaults. Existing routes and legacy URL redirects remain available when their Cargo features are enabled. The configuration file format is unchanged apart from the keys and substitution syntax below.

Review the [database versions](<#postgresql-sources-need-postgresql-15-and-postgis-35>), [`martin cp`](<#martin-cp-is-now-martin-cp>), the [terminal dashboard](<#the-terminal-dashboard-is-on-by-default>), the [web UI](<#the-web-ui-is-served-to-localhost-by-default>), [archive tile caching](<#pmtiles-and-mbtiles-tiles-attach-the-cache-control-header-by-default>), [cache keys](<#cache-sizes-have-one-spelling>), the [MBTiles schema](<#normalized-mbtiles-files-use-tiles_shallow-and-tiles_data>) and the [Docker images](<#docker-images-have-no-shell-and-run-as-a-non-root-user>) even if 1.x showed no deprecation warnings.

### `martin-cp` is now `martin cp`

Replace `martin-cp` with `martin cp` in scripts and commands. The copy options and configuration file still apply, subject to the changes below. Release tarballs, Docker and Homebrew no longer include a separate `martin-cp` binary. The `mbtiles` binary keeps its name and loses its hidden `--verbose` flag, which did nothing. Use `RUST_LOG` to control logging.

```bash
# 1.x
martin-cp --output-file tileset.mbtiles --source my_source postgres://postgres@localhost/db
# 2.0
martin cp --output-file tileset.mbtiles --source my_source postgres://postgres@localhost/db
```

See [Generating Tiles in Bulk](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-cp/index.md>).

### `mbtiles` is released separately

The Martin release archives and Debian package contain only `martin`. Get `mbtiles` from the `mbtiles-<target>` archives on the [`mbtiles-v*` releases](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases?q=mbtiles-v&expanded=true>), with `cargo binstall mbtiles`, or from the Docker image, which still includes it.

See [MBTiles tool](<https://maplibre.org/martin/mbtiles/index.md>).

### The terminal dashboard is on by default

Remove `--tui`. Martin now shows the dashboard when stdout is a terminal. Use `--no-tui` for the log stream instead. When stdout is not a terminal, as in a service or pipe, Martin keeps the plain log automatically.

The dashboard's log pane follows `RUST_LOG_FORMAT` and defaults to `pretty`.

See [Terminal dashboard](<https://maplibre.org/martin/run-with-cli/index.md>).

### The web UI is served to localhost by default

`--webui` now defaults to `enable` instead of `disable`. Loopback clients get the web UI at `/`. Other clients get the same text response as with `disable`. Set `--webui disable` or `web_ui: disable` to restore the 1.x behavior. `--webui enable-for-all` is unchanged.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Reverse proxies and containers**
>
> Martin checks the TCP peer address, ignoring forwarded headers. A proxy connecting over loopback exposes the web UI to its clients unless you set `--webui disable`. With Docker bridge networking, connections from the host are not loopback. Use `--webui enable-for-all` to expose the UI as described in [Running with Docker](<https://maplibre.org/martin/run-with-docker/index.md>).

### PMTiles and MBTiles tiles attach the `Cache-Control` header by default

When no `cache_control` is configured, PMTiles and MBTiles tiles have `max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=86400` by default. 1.x sent no `Cache-Control` header for them. This means that a returning visitor's browser can now use tiles which are assumed to be static and only checks them with the server in the background. A server side rewritten archive may only show up on the visitor's next load due to invalidation if the tiles are cached on the client and the `stale-while-revalidate`-check in the background suggests that the tiles martin offers are stale.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Set `cache_control: no-cache` for browsers to check before drawing it**
>
> A top-level or per-source `cache_control` replaces this default.
>
> ```yaml
> cache_control: no-cache
> ```
>
> See [Tile Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-tiles/index.md>).

### PostgreSQL sources need PostgreSQL 15 and PostGIS 3.5

Martin 2.0 refuses to start against older databases, where 1.x accepted PostgreSQL 11 and PostGIS 3.0. Upgrade the database before upgrading Martin.

| Requirement | 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | 11 | 15 |
| PostGIS | 3.0 | 3.5 |

PostgreSQL 12, 13 and 14 are end-of-life, and PostGIS 3.5 fixes geometry that older versions hid on some zoom levels.

### PostgreSQL settings come from the command line or the configuration file

Replace these environment variables with command-line options or configuration keys.

| 1.x environment variable | 2.0 command line | 2.0 configuration file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | the connection string as a positional argument | `postgres.connection_string` |
| `DEFAULT_SRID` | `--default-srid` | `postgres.default_srid` |
| `PGSSLCERT` | `--ssl-cert` | `postgres.ssl_cert` |
| `PGSSLKEY` | `--ssl-key` | `postgres.ssl_key` |
| `PGSSLROOTCERT` | `--ca-root-file` | `postgres.ssl_root_cert` |

Martin ignores the old variables. Starting with only `DATABASE_URL` exported fails with `No tile sources found`. On grids with a coordinate reference system, auto-discovered tables with SRID 0 are skipped with a warning unless you set `default_srid`. Simple grids use SRID 0 and need no fallback. Client certificates previously supplied through `PGSSLCERT` are not sent unless you configure them explicitly.

```bash
# 1.x
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@localhost/db
martin
# 2.0
martin postgres://postgres@localhost/db
```

To keep using an environment variable, reference it in the configuration file. See [Configuration](<https://maplibre.org/martin/config-file/index.md>) for the substitution syntax.

```yaml
postgres:
  connection_string: ${DATABASE_URL}
```

With Docker, pass the connection string after the image name or pass the variable to a mounted configuration file.

```bash
# 1.x
docker run -p 3000:3000 -e DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@postgres.example.org/db ghcr.io/maplibre/martin
# 2.0
docker run -p 3000:3000 ghcr.io/maplibre/martin postgres://postgres@postgres.example.org/db
# 2.0, keeping the variable
docker run -p 3000:3000 -e DATABASE_URL -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/config.yaml" ghcr.io/maplibre/martin --config /config.yaml
```

See [Environment Variables](<https://maplibre.org/martin/env-vars/index.md>) and [SSL Connections](<https://maplibre.org/martin/pg-connections/index.md#ssl-connections>).

### Default values in the configuration file use `${VAR:-default}`

Replace `${VAR:default}` with `${VAR:-default}`. The old syntax fails at startup with a substitution error.

```yaml
# 1.x
connection_string: ${DATABASE_URL:postgres://postgres@localhost/db}
# 2.0
connection_string: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://postgres@localhost/db}
```

### Cache sizes have one spelling

Replace the old cache keys below. Martin reports them as unrecognized and ignores their values, so a cache can fall back to its default size. Most migrated silently in 1.x unless both spellings were set. `pmtiles.dir_cache_size_mb` was already ignored with a deprecation warning.

| 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `cache_size_mb` | `cache.size_mb` |
| `tile_cache_size_mb` | `cache.tile_size_mb` |
| `fonts.cache_size_mb` | `fonts.cache.size_mb` |
| `sprites.cache_size_mb` | `sprites.cache.size_mb` |
| `pmtiles.directory_cache_size_mb` | `pmtiles.directory_cache.size_mb` |
| `pmtiles.dir_cache_size_mb` | `pmtiles.directory_cache.size_mb` |

```yaml
# 1.x
cache_size_mb: 1024
pmtiles:
  directory_cache_size_mb: 128
# 2.0
cache:
  size_mb: 1024
pmtiles:
  directory_cache:
    size_mb: 128
```

See the `cache` section of the [full configuration](<https://maplibre.org/martin/config-file/index.md#full-configuration>).

### Object storage options use their `object_store` names

Replace these legacy settings with configuration keys directly under `pmtiles` or `cog`. Old environment variables are ignored silently. Old configuration keys are reported as unrecognized.

| 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `AWS_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=1`, `aws_s3_force_path_style: true`, `force_path_style: true` | `virtual_hosted_style_request: false` (the meaning is inverted) |
| `AWS_SKIP_CREDENTIALS=1`, `AWS_NO_CREDENTIALS=1`, `aws_skip_credentials: true`, `aws_no_credentials: true` | `skip_signature: true` |
| `AWS_PROFILE=name` | `profile: name` |

The standard `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` and `AWS_REGION` variables still work.

```yaml
pmtiles:
  skip_signature: true
  sources:
    tiles: s3://public-bucket/tiles.pmtiles
```

A public bucket previously accessed with `AWS_SKIP_CREDENTIALS=1` can now fail during instance credential lookup outside AWS. The error does not name the removed variable. Set `skip_signature: true` for unsigned requests. This requires a configuration file, including when replacing a command such as `martin s3://public-bucket/tiles.pmtiles`.

See [Remote files and prefixes](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pmtiles/index.md#remote-files-and-prefixes>).

### Plain `http://` sources must opt in

Set `allow_http: true` in the configuration file for PMTiles or COG sources using `http://`. It now defaults to `false`, so plain HTTP sources are refused at startup with an error naming the option. HTTPS URLs are unaffected.

```yaml
pmtiles:
  allow_http: true
  sources:
    tiles: http://tiles.internal/tiles.pmtiles
```

The bare command `martin http://tiles.internal/tiles.pmtiles` needs a configuration file to enable `allow_http`.

See [HTTP(S)](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pmtiles/index.md#https>).

### Normalized MBTiles files use `tiles_shallow` and `tiles_data`

New files created with `mbtiles copy --dst-type normalized` or `martin cp --mbtiles-type normalized` use `tiles_shallow` and `tiles_data`, the layout [Planetiler](<https://github.com/onthegomap/planetiler>) writes. This is also the `martin cp` default. Both layouts expose the standard `tiles` view, so readers using that view keep working.

Existing `map` and `images` files remain readable. Copying one to a new file without `--dst-type` preserves its schema. The CLI no longer offers that layout when converting from another schema.

New normalized files have no per-tile hashes or `tiles_with_hash` view. `mbtiles validate` checks tile references instead. `agg_tiles_hash` still covers the content. Choose `flat-with-hash` if you need per-tile hashes.

See [MBTiles Schemas](<https://maplibre.org/martin/mbtiles-schema/index.md#normalized>).

### Rendering is not part of the default build

For server-side style rendering on Linux, use the `-full` Docker image (`:latest-full` or `:<version>-full`), a `-full` Linux-gnu tarball, or `cargo install martin --features rendering`. The default builds no longer include rendering.

Rendering is stable as of 2.0. The configuration is unchanged. Set `styles.rendering: true` to enable it, or keep your existing rendering options.

See [Server-side raster tile rendering](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/index.md>) and [Installation](<https://maplibre.org/martin/installation/index.md>).

### Rendering uses mln-rs instead of MapLibre Native's C++ core

Martin 2.0 renders with [mln-rs](<https://github.com/louwers/mln-rs>), a Rust rewrite of MapLibre Native. mln-rs brings static rendering to more platforms, renders more tiles per second with several workers, and uses less memory. Because mln-rs is written in Rust, memory-safety bugs are less likely to crash Martin.

The main reason for the switch is [GHSA-5xxm-54w8-h85j](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/security/advisories/GHSA-5xxm-54w8-h85j>): Martin 1.x rendered through Vulkan by default, and concurrent render requests could crash the server. Martin 2.0 renders through OpenGL ES by default. To pick another graphics backend, see [Graphics backend](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/index.md#graphics-backend>).

### Static images follow the style's projection

Martin 2.0 draws a static image of a style that sets `"projection": {"type": "globe"}` as a globe, as MapLibre GL JS does. Martin 1.x drew every static image in Web Mercator. Raster tiles and [OGC API - Maps](<https://maplibre.org/martin/ogc-api/index.md#maps>) images still draw in Web Mercator.

To keep flat static images, remove `projection` from the style or set it to `{"type": "mercator"}`.

### x86\_64 binaries require an x86-64-v3 CPU

The prebuilt x86\_64 binaries, Debian package and Docker images are built for the x86-64-v3 feature level (AVX2, BMI2, FMA; Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator, 2015 or newer). On older CPUs they fail with an illegal instruction error. aarch64 builds are unaffected.

To run Martin on an older CPU, use the `martin-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl-legacycpu.tar.gz` release asset or the `:latest-legacycpu` Docker image, or [build it from source](<https://maplibre.org/martin/development/index.md>) without `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`.

### Docker images have no shell and run as a non-root user

The Docker images contain Martin and the [Wolfi](<https://wolfi.dev>) packages Martin loads, on an empty `scratch` base. They have no shell and no package manager, and run as a non-root user. Image scanners such as Trivy report fewer vulnerabilities because the images contain fewer packages.

|  | 1.x | 2.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | Ubuntu 24.04 | Wolfi packages on `scratch` |
| User | `root` | `nonroot`, uid and gid `65532` |
| `HEALTHCHECK` | `wget --spider http://127.0.0.1:3000/health` | `martin health` |
| Shell, `apt-get` | yes | no |
| Tags | `:<version>`, `:latest` | also `:2` and `:2.0`, which every stable release moves |

The `-full` and `-legacycpu` variants get the same tags with their suffix, such as `:2-full`. Update your setup if it relies on any of the following 1.x behaviors:

- **Shell health checks.** A health check that runs a shell command, such as `wget --spider ...` or any `docker run --health-cmd`, fails with `exec: "/bin/sh": ... no such file or directory`. Remove it and rely on the image's `HEALTHCHECK`. If Martin listens on a port other than `3000`, set `MARTIN_HEALTH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health`. See [Health Check](<https://maplibre.org/martin/run-with-docker/index.md#health-check>) for what `martin health` checks. A health check of your own must run `martin health` in exec form:

  ```yaml
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/martin", "health", "--url", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/health"]
  ```
- **Writing to bind mounts.** Martin runs as uid `65532`, so it fails with a permission error when it writes into a bind-mounted directory that this uid cannot write to. This affects the output of `martin cp` and `--save-config`. Run the container as your own user with `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`, or as root with `--user 0` as in 1.x. Files that Martin serves must be readable by the user the container runs as.
- **Derived images.** A Dockerfile that starts `FROM ghcr.io/maplibre/martin` cannot `RUN` commands, because the image has no shell. Copy the binaries into your own base image instead:

  ```dockerfile
  FROM your-base-image
  COPY --from=ghcr.io/maplibre/martin:2 /usr/local/bin/martin /usr/local/bin/
  ```

  The default binaries need glibc 2.39 or newer. The `-full` binary also needs Mesa's `libEGL.so.1`. The `-legacycpu` binaries are static and need no shared libraries.
- **Interactive shells.** `docker exec <container> sh` fails because the image has no shell. Binaries in the image still run, such as `docker exec <container> /usr/local/bin/martin health`. To inspect a running container with a shell, use `docker debug <container>`, which needs Docker Desktop.

### Cargo features were merged

If you build Martin or `martin-core` yourself with `--features` or `--no-default-features`, rename the features:

| 1.x features | 2.0 feature |
| --- | --- |
| `fonts`, `sprites`, `styles` | `resources` |
| `hillshade`, `contour`, `geojson` | `processing` |
| `mlt` | none, always enabled |
| `unstable-cog` | `cog` |

All are enabled by default, so default builds, release binaries and Docker images keep their features and now also serve [COG sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-cog-files/index.md>). `metrics`, `webui`, `tui`, `lambda` and the source features `postgres`, `pmtiles`, `mbtiles` and `passthrough` keep their names.

```bash
# 1.x
cargo install martin --locked --no-default-features --features postgres,fonts,sprites,styles
# 2.0
cargo install martin --locked --no-default-features --features postgres,resources
```

### For users of the crates

- In `martin-tile-utils`, `TileCoord` fields are private. Construct coordinates with `TileCoord::new_checked` or `TileCoord::new_unchecked` and read them with `z()`, `x()` and `y()`.
- `TileData` is now `bytes::Bytes` instead of `Vec<u8>`, including data returned by `mbtiles::Mbtiles::stream_tiles`.
- In `martin-core`, `Source` is no longer dyn compatible. Its `clone_source` and `cancel_registry` methods were removed. Sources use the closed `AnySource` enum, and `BoxedSource` is now `Arc<AnySource>`. With the `postgres` feature, call `cancel_registry()` on `AnySource` or `BoxedSource`.
- `CatalogSourceEntry` gained `tile_grid`, `PostgresSource::new` requires the source's `TileGrid`, and `CogError::TooManyImages` was removed.
- `mbtiles::Mbtiles::insert_tiles` now requires tile data to implement `Sync`. The copier writes the normalized layout described above.

See the [martin-core](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/blob/main/crates/martin-core/CHANGELOG.md>) and [mbtiles](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/blob/main/crates/mbtiles/CHANGELOG.md>) changelogs for crate releases.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](<https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/>), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](<https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html>).

## \[Unreleased\]

## [2.0.0-beta.8](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/compare/martin-v2.0.0-beta.7...martin-v2.0.0-beta.8>) - 2026-11-25

> \[!NOTE\] This is the eighth beta of Martin 2.0. It has one breaking change relative to [2.0.0-beta.7](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases/tag/martin-v2.0.0-beta.7>), listed below. If you are coming from 1.x, read the [migration guide](<https://maplibre.org/martin/migration-guide/>) first.

### Breaking changes

- A build from a git checkout embeds a placeholder page instead of the web UI until `just ui::build` has run. The UI now comes prebuilt from the new `martin-ui` crate, so `cargo install martin` no longer needs Node.js, and without source maps the embedded UI shrinks from 8.5 MB to 2.6 MB. Release binaries and Docker images are unchanged ([\#3939](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3939>)).

### Added

- `martin cp --mode bulk` reads OpenStreetMap `.osm.pbf` extracts from a new `osm:` section, with the same `layers` as table sources ([\#3954](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3954>), [\#3967](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3967>), [\#3977](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3977>), [\#3978](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3978>)). See [OpenStreetMap PBF Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-osm/>). A closed way is a polygon unless `area=no`, and also a line unless `area=yes`, as in Planetiler. `relations:` names sets of relations whose tags, `id` and `role` the members read as `relations.<set>`, and every feature has an integer `osm_id`. On a Germany extract (4.9 GB, 24 threads), a run took 3 min 15 s and 9.5 GB of memory for 241,142 tiles. The tile server does not serve `osm` sources.
- A new `shapefile:` section reads ESRI shapefiles (`.shp`, or a `.zip` holding one, in EPSG:4326 or EPSG:3857). They render in one run together with `osm` sources, but not with database sources ([\#3971](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3971>), [\#3972](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3972>)). See [Shapefile Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-shapefile/>).
- Two basemap recipes build from an extract and the ocean polygons ([\#3956](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3956>), [\#3966](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3966>), [\#3967](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3967>), [\#3968](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3968>), [\#3969](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3969>), [\#3970](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3970>), [\#3971](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3971>), [\#3972](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3972>), [\#3978](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3978>)): [Shortbread](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-osm-basemap/>) (`shortbread.yaml`) matches all 67 examples of Planetiler's `shortbread.spec.yml` and builds Germany in 2m 54s with 19.1 GB of memory. [OpenMapTiles](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-osm-openmaptiles/>) has all 16 layers, matches 231 of Planetiler's 341 layer-test examples, and builds Berlin in 1m 8s against Planetiler's 1m 19s.
- `martin test` tests `osm` and `shapefile` sources of a configuration without a `postgres` section. Each case is one object of the file, with its feature id as `id` and its WKT as `geometry` ([\#3955](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3955>), [\#3972](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3972>)). See [OpenStreetMap sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-test/#openstreetmap-sources>).
- Several `layers` can write into one output layer by naming it in `layer`. Before, a duplicate name was refused. They must agree on `extent`, `sort_by` and per-tile operations ([\#3973](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3973>)). See [Combining layers](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/#combining-layers>).
- `geometry` can be a list, such as `[point, polygon_point_on_surface]`, and each feature is drawn by the first entry that takes its type. `polygon_point_on_surface` and `polygon_centroid_if_convex` are no longer refused ([\#3968](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3968>), [\#3969](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3969>), [\#3970](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3970>)). See [Geometry](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/#geometry>).
- Layer expressions take `area(unit)` on a spherical Earth with Planetiler's units, `matches`, `regex.replace`, `min`, `max`, `list.min()`, `list.max()`, and Planetiler's `isLatin` and `removeLatin`. A `where` that calls them is checked in Martin, not in PostgreSQL, and `area` is not available in `where` ([\#3956](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3956>), [\#3966](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3966>), [\#3974](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3974>), [\#3977](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3977>)). See [Expressions](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/#expressions>).
- Grid `thinning` can write each kept point's place in its square to a `rank` attribute, as OpenMapTiles' `place` layer does, and then needs no `limit`. An attribute with `hidden: true` can be read by per-tile operations but is left out of the tile and `vector_layers` ([\#3975](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3975>), [\#3976](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3976>)). See [`thinning`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/#thinning>) and [hidden attributes](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/#hidden-attributes>).
- `convert_to_mlt` takes `profile` (`web` by default, `native`, `min-size`, `diffable`, `fast-encoding`) and `network` (`offline` by default, `3g`, `4g`, `5g`), which pick the encoder defaults the other keys override, and `tessellate: auto` keeps only the triangles that pay off on that network. The defaults encode as before ([\#3985](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3985>)). See [Tuning the Encoder](<https://maplibre.org/martin/postprocessing/mlt/#tuning-the-encoder>).
- The web UI edits styles in a built-in editor instead of an embedded Maputnik, with a layer list, the live map, and Layer, Palette and Checks tabs. Attribute names and example values come from the tile source, the Palette tab recolors every layer using a color, and Checks reports low-contrast labels and spec errors. Edits stay in the browser until you download the style JSON. Catalogs show their count as the heading and tile formats by name, such as MVT ([\#3938](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3938>), [\#4044](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4044>)). See [Style Sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/>).
- A contour tile beyond the elevation source's depth is traced from the nearest ancestor tile, upsampled bilinearly, with the requested zoom's interval. Before, it answered `204`. With Mapterhorn at `maxzoom: 17`, Kilimanjaro now answers `200` at z13 instead of `204` ([\#3981](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/3981>), [\#3989](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3989>)). See [Variable-depth sources](<https://maplibre.org/martin/postprocessing/contour/#variable-depth-sources>).
- Rendering uses MapLibre Native through the prebuilt `maplibre-native-ffi` library. Building with `rendering` needs no system packages, and the `-full` image needs 3 runtime packages instead of 8. A renderer that does not answer within a minute is dropped, and MapLibre logs under the `maplibre_native` target ([\#3849](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3849>), [\#3963](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3963>)). See [Logs](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/#logs>).
- `mbtiles diff --patch-type zstd-raw` and `zstd-gz` store each changed tile as zstd compressed against the old tile. On Germany Shortbread pairs the patches are as small as `bin-diff-*` ones and take 175 to 570 times less CPU to create. `mbtiles copy --apply-patch` reads them ([\#4067](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4067>)). See [Binary diff support](<https://maplibre.org/martin/mbtiles-diff/#binary-diff-support>).

### Fixed

- `martin cp --mode bulk` follows the same configuration as tile mode ([\#3940](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3940>), [\#3941](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3941>), [\#3942](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3942>), [\#3943](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3943>), [\#3944](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3944>), [\#3987](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3987>)). See [Generating Tilesets](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/>). It refuses a connection `tile_grid` other than Web Mercator, and `convert_to_mlt: disabled` without `--format mvt`. Tables without `layers` follow `order_by`. Without `--bbox`, it renders only the tiles touching the sources' `bounds` and writes their union as `bounds`, where it rendered the whole world. The table comment's TileJSON metadata and `compression` are kept. Web Mercator tables scan at zoom 0 without PostGIS 3.5 failing on the poles. Before, it ignored each of these.
- `martin cp --mode bulk` gives each property key one MLT column type in every tile of a layer, so `3` in one tile and `"n/a"` in another are both strings, with one warning. Integers rounded into a float column are warned about, and an encode error names its layer and tile ([\#3982](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3982>), [\#3983](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3983>)).
- GeoJSON sources keep polygons that clipping and snapping turned inside out. Before, such a polygon was dropped or served as a sliver: at z0 to 4, up to 55 French communes per tile were missing ([\#4010](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/4010>), [\#4011](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4011>)).
- `where: '!(f > 1.0)'` keeps rows where `f` is NaN, in Martin and in the SQL pushed to PostgreSQL alike (`cel` 0.16) ([\#3994](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3994>)).
- `martin test` compares float attributes up to a relative difference of 1e-9, so a spec recorded on Linux passes on macOS ([\#4036](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4036>)). `martin test generate` finds its own cases again, and paths are named `` `where` is false `` without repeating the expression, so rerun `generate` on older spec files ([\#3956](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3956>)).
- `mbtiles diff` and `mbtiles copy --apply-patch` are linear on normalized and flat-with-hash files. Before, joining their `tiles` view was quadratic: a one-day Germany diff of a normalized file extrapolated to 58 h and now takes 4 s ([\#4066](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4066>)).
- `actix-http` 3.22.0 fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0552, RUSTSEC-2026-0553 and RUSTSEC-2026-0554, and `url` 2.5.9 fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0592, which a STAC API could trigger through `cog.stac` sources ([\#3990](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3990>), [\#4052](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4052>)).

### Performance

- A free render worker prefers requests for a renderer it already holds, and waits at most the measured switch cost for one. For static images with 2 styles at `@1x`/`@2x` on 8 workers, throughput went from 39.4 to 82.8 req/s. Static workers keep 2 renderers each instead of 1, set by the new `static_renderers_per_worker` ([\#4006](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4006>)). See [Request scheduling](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/#request-scheduling>).
- Table sources cast the tile envelope once per tile instead of once per feature, serving 4-5% more z14 road and POI tiles per second on PostGIS 3.7.0. With 1,004 tables, table discovery takes 21% less time ([\#3935](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3935>), [\#3958](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3958>)).
- Without `network`, `martin cp --mode bulk` encodes compressed MLT tiles for `4g` instead of `offline`, as FSST and FastPFOR cost bytes under gzip. Germany z2-14 as gzip MBTiles went from 3361 to 3108 MB (-7.5%) ([\#3988](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3988>)).
- `agg_tiles_hash` is computed by reading tiles in key order instead of sorting every blob in SQLite: `mbtiles validate` on Germany went from 22 to 7 s, which also speeds up `diff` and `apply-patch`. An empty file hashed with `fnv1a-decimal` now gets the right hash ([\#4068](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4068>)).

### Unstable

> \[!WARNING\] None of this is in the release binaries. It needs a build with `--features unstable-mlt-v2` or `--features unstable-duckdb`, and its configuration may still change.

- `martin cp --mode bulk --format mlt2` writes the MLT v2 wire format, reads the v2-only `convert_to_mlt` keys `allow_delta2` and `allow_rans_vertices`, and keeps a `jsonb` column whole as one nested column ([\#3986](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3986>), [\#4026](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4026>), [\#4027](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4027>), [\#4029](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4029>), [\#4030](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4030>)). In every build, MLT v2 tiles are detected as MLT instead of MVT.
- Remote GeoParquet reads stay in DuckDB 2.0's file cache. On the file from [\#4007](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/4007>), a warm tile went from 15 GETs and 94 MiB to none, and p50 from 1.25 to 0.24 s. DuckDB 1.5 is no longer supported ([\#4057](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4057>)).

### Other

- *(docs)* "Martin" for what the software does, "you" for what the reader does, and a `render-tileserver` example in martin-core ([\#3979](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3979>), [\#4043](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4043>))
- *(deps)* web UI dependencies with `maplibre-gl` 6.18, the Docker base images, `mlt-core` 0.23, `notify` 9, `zip` 9.6, `actix-web` 4.20 and `pmtiles` 0.28.1, with `cql2` vendored as `martin-vendored-cql2` ([\#3932](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3932>), [\#3933](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3933>), [\#3952](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3952>), [\#3960](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3960>), [\#3961](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3961>), [\#3992](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3992>), [\#3993](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3993>), [\#3999](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3999>), [\#4008](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4008>), [\#4045](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4045>), [\#4048](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4048>), [\#4051](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4051>), [\#4056](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4056>), [\#4060](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4060>), [\#4061](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4061>))
- *(ci)* faster CI, with every crate moved under `crates/` ([\#3937](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3937>), [\#4009](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4009>), [\#4032](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4032>), [\#4037](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4037>), [\#4038](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4038>), [\#4039](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4039>), [\#4040](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4040>), [\#4042](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4042>), [\#4054](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4054>), [\#4058](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4058>), [\#4059](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4059>), [\#4070](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/4070>))

## [2.0.0-beta.7](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/compare/martin-v2.0.0-beta.6...martin-v2.0.0-beta.7>) - 2026-11-11

> \[!NOTE\] This is the seventh beta of Martin 2.0. It has three breaking changes relative to [2.0.0-beta.6](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases/tag/martin-v2.0.0-beta.6>), listed below. If you are coming from 1.x, read the [migration guide](<https://maplibre.org/martin/migration-guide/>) first.

### Breaking changes

- The Martin release archives and the Debian package contain only `martin`. `mbtiles` is attached to the `mbtiles-v*` releases instead, as `mbtiles-<target>` archives with their own SBOM, and the Docker image still includes both ([\#3917](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3917>)). See [`mbtiles` is released separately](<https://maplibre.org/martin/migration-guide/#mbtiles-is-released-separately>).
- The `maplibre/martin` Homebrew tap is no longer updated. `brew install martin` installs the [homebrew-core formula](<https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/martin>), which follows stable releases only ([\#3918](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3918>)). Switch with `brew uninstall martin && brew untap maplibre/martin && brew install martin`. See [installation](<https://maplibre.org/martin/installation/>).
- The derived `geometry` values of table `layers` have Planetiler's names: `centroid_if_convex` is now `polygon_centroid_if_convex`, `label_point` is gone, and `polygon_centroid`, `line_centroid`, `polygon_point_on_surface` and `point_on_line` are new ([\#3913](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3913>)).

### Added

- Table [`layers`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/#per-tile-operations>) take per-tile operations, which act on a layer's whole feature list in one tile, after `sort_by`: `merge_lines` joins lines whose ends meet, `merge_polygons` unions a group's polygons, `thinning` drops features crowded out by earlier ones (`method: grid`, `distance` or `tile`), `merge_multi` combines a group into one multi-feature, and `limit` keeps the first `count` features ([\#3902](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3902>), [\#3903](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3903>), [\#3904](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3904>), [\#3905](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3905>), [\#3906](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3906>), [\#3907](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3907>)). Each one can take different settings per zoom range, and a bulk run logs what each did. They work in bulk mode and when `layers` are served. The configuration of `layers` may still change.

```yaml
layers:
  pois:
    sort_by: [rank]
    thinning: { method: grid, size: 64, limit: 1 }
    limit:
      - { maxzoom: 10, count: 50 }
      - { minzoom: 11, count: 200 }
```

- `geometry: polygon_centroid`, `line_centroid` and `centroid` draw a feature as its centroid point. Before, they were refused ([\#3920](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3920>)).
- `martin cp --mode bulk` shows each stage, a progress bar with an ETA and how busy the merge, encode and write threads are, updated every 250 ms. Without a terminal, it still logs every 10 s ([\#3911](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3911>), [\#3931](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3931>)). See [Generating Tilesets](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/>).
- The web UI is redesigned, with fixes for mobile layouts, dark mode and contrast. Tile thumbnails load only once their card is near the viewport, at most 4 at a time ([\#3921](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3921>), [\#3922](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3922>)).
- When `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `~/.cache` are not writable, as in a read-only container, rendering keeps Mesa's shader cache in a temporary directory until Martin exits. With renderers being replaced, a request went from 622 to 108 ms ([\#3898](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3898>)). See [Shader cache](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/#shader-cache>).

### Fixed

- `mbtiles diff` computes a missing `agg_tiles_hash` instead of refusing, so every diff records the hash before and after. `mbtiles apply-patch` and `mbtiles copy --apply-patch` check the base file's hash first, and `apply-patch` rolls back when the result does not match. `apply-patch --validate` recomputes the base hash instead of trusting the stored one ([\#1244](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/1244>), [\#3916](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3916>)). See [Diffing MBTiles](<https://maplibre.org/martin/mbtiles-diff/>).
- A local PMTiles archive renamed over a source while it opens is noticed on the first read, and the source reloads. Before, the old file was served until the next change ([\#3897](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3897>)).
- `actix-http` 3.20.3 and `actix-web` 4.18.2 fix RUSTSEC-2026-0446, RUSTSEC-2026-0447 and RUSTSEC-2026-0448 ([\#3912](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3912>)).

### Performance

- Local PMTiles archives bigger than memory are served without the 2.0 slowdown, by reading the file instead of a memory map. On OpenFreeMap's 87 GB planet on a c8g.xlarge, Martin served 11,000 tiles/s at p99 under 50 ms, against 1,750 for 2.0.0-beta.4 and 5,500 for 1.16.1 ([\#3858](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3858>)). A local archive is checked for changes at most once a second, off the async workers, so a changed archive is noticed up to a second later ([\#3900](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3900>)).
- A connection waiting on a slow client keeps a reference to the tile instead of its own copy. With 1,000 stalled clients on Berlin's 50 largest tiles, memory per client fell from 193 KB to 12.5 KB (`actix-http` 3.21.0) ([\#3923](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3923>)).

### Unstable

> \[!WARNING\] None of this is in the release binaries. It needs a build with `--features unstable-duckdb`, and its configuration may still change.

- DuckDB S3 secrets are built from the same options as the object store. `aws_endpoint_url_s3` always wins over `aws_endpoint`, and `skip_signature` also accepts `on`, `yes` and `y` ([\#3872](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3872>)).
- A directory given on the command line no longer fails as an unrecognizable connection. Before, DuckDB skipping it undid the claim of the file sources before it ([\#3893](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3893>)).

### Other

- *(docs)* schema examples for the optional DuckDB fields ([\#3894](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3894>))
- *(ci)* more reliable CI and release PRs ([\#3892](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3892>), [\#3896](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3896>), [\#3899](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3899>), [\#3924](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3924>), [\#3925](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3925>), [\#3930](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3930>))

## [2.0.0-beta.6](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/compare/martin-v2.0.0-beta.5...martin-v2.0.0-beta.6>) - 2026-11-04

> \[!NOTE\] This is the sixth beta of Martin 2.0. It has one breaking change relative to [2.0.0-beta.5](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases/tag/martin-v2.0.0-beta.5>), listed below. If you are coming from 1.x, read the [migration guide](<https://maplibre.org/martin/migration-guide/>) first.

### Breaking changes

- The `unstable-generate` cargo feature is gone. Bulk mode, table `layers` and `martin test` are built with `postgres`, which now also enables `mbtiles` ([\#3891](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3891>)). Builds that pass `--features unstable-generate` fail and pass `postgres` instead. Default builds, release binaries and Docker images need no change.

### Added

- The release binaries and Docker images include [`martin cp --mode bulk`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/>), which reads each table once and builds the whole tileset itself, as MBTiles or PMTiles. They also include table [`layers`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-pg-layers/>) and [`martin test`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-test/>) ([\#3891](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3891>)). On a Germany extract (zooms 0 to 14, 16 threads), bulk mode built a tileset with one layer per table in under 2 minutes, where tile mode took about 20. PostgreSQL used about 100 CPU seconds instead of 10,300. With `layers`, the same data takes about 1 minute. `--mode auto` still picks `tile`, and the configuration of `layers` may still change.

```bash
martin cp --mode bulk --output-file germany.pmtiles --max-zoom 14 postgres://localhost/osm
```

- Release archives include an SPDX SBOM, `martin.spdx.json` ([\#3888](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3888>)). Each release also has a `provenance.json` attestation bundle, so `gh attestation verify --bundle` checks a download without network access. See [installation](<https://maplibre.org/martin/installation/>) ([\#3874](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3874>)).

### Fixed

- `mbtiles summary`, and `mbtiles copy` from an MBTiles file without a unique tile index, print a warning instead of failing. `mbtiles copy` adds the index to its output, so it repairs the file. Martin logs a warning when it serves such a file, and writing into one still fails ([\#782](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/782>), [\#3870](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/3870>), [\#3871](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3871>)).

### Unstable

> \[!WARNING\] None of this is in the release binaries. It needs a build with `--features unstable-duckdb`, and its configuration may still change.

- DuckDB sources work with DuckDB 2.0. Before, discovery failed on it and auto-publish found no tables ([\#3864](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3864>)).

### Other

- *(deps)* update `pmtiles` to 0.26, `duckdb` to allow 2.0, `vt100` to 0.18, `hotpath`, `maplibre-gl` to 6.16 and the frontend's npm dependencies, the PostGIS image, the pre-commit hooks and the GitHub Actions, and drop the last crates still on `syn` 1 and the `wkb` git patch ([\#3879](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3879>), [\#3860](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3860>), [\#3865](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3865>), [\#3878](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3878>), [\#3863](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3863>), [\#3880](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3880>), [\#3875](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3875>), [\#3876](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3876>), [\#3877](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3877>), [\#3862](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3862>), [\#3881](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3881>), [\#3854](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3854>), [\#3853](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3853>), [\#3883](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3883>), [\#3890](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3890>))
- *(ci)* more reliable CI ([\#3866](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3866>), [\#3867](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3867>), [\#3884](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3884>), [\#3885](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3885>))

## [2.0.0-beta.5](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/compare/martin-v2.0.0-beta.4...martin-v2.0.0-beta.5>) - 2026-10-29

> \[!NOTE\] This is the fifth beta of Martin 2.0. It has one breaking change relative to [2.0.0-beta.4](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/releases/tag/martin-v2.0.0-beta.4>), listed below. If you are coming from 1.x, read the [migration guide](<https://maplibre.org/martin/migration-guide/>) first.

### Breaking changes

- Rendered WebP tiles and static images are lossy at quality 80 instead of lossless, and JPEG goes from quality 75 to 80 ([\#3813](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3813>)). The median rendered WebP tile went from 62.6 KB to 10.3 KB. Bytes and `ETag`s change once on upgrade. Set `styles.rendering.quality: { webp: lossless, jpeg: 75 }` for the previous output. See [quality](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-styles/rendering/#quality>).

### Added

- Martin serves its tiles, styles and rendered maps through the [OGC API](<https://maplibre.org/martin/ogc-api/>) under `/ogc`, for tools that only speak OGC, such as GDAL. It is in the default build, as the `ogcapi` feature. OGC API - Tiles serves every tile source as a collection, with tilesets and tile matrix sets ([\#3763](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3763>), [\#3764](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3764>)). OGC API - Styles lists the styles ([\#3800](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3800>)), and `/ogc/api` serves the OpenAPI 3.1 definition ([\#3801](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3801>)). With rendering enabled, OGC API - Maps draws styles and raster sources as PNG, JPEG or GeoTIFF images and map tiles ([\#3802](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3802>), [\#3803](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3803>), [\#3804](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3804>), [\#3805](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3805>), [\#3806](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3806>)). The official OGC test suites run against Martin in CI ([\#3765](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3765>), [\#3771](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3771>), [\#3799](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3799>)).
- `cog.stac` serves the imagery a STAC API such as [Earth Search](<https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1>) finds for each tile as one source, reprojected from each scene's UTM zone to Web Mercator ([\#3814](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3814>), [\#3815](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3815>), [\#3816](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3816>)). See [Imagery from a STAC API](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-cog-files/#imagery-from-a-stac-api>).

```yaml
cog:
  aws_request_payer: true
  stac:
    naip:
      url: https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1
      collection: naip
      asset: image
      minzoom: 13
```

- `cog.tile_index` serves the COGs a `gdaltindex` GeoPackage lists as one source ([\#3820](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3820>)). See [Imagery listed by a tile index](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-cog-files/#imagery-listed-by-a-tile-index>) and the [NAIP recipe](<https://maplibre.org/martin/recipe-cog-naip/>).
- COG sources re-encode their tiles with `format` (`png`, `webp` or `jpeg`), `quality` and `background` ([\#3822](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3822>), [\#3823](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3823>)). WebP at quality 80 is 5 to 12 times smaller than PNG on NAIP. See [Tile format](<https://maplibre.org/martin/sources-cog-files/#tile-format>).
- COGs stored in uncompressed strips are served, cut into 256 px tiles, and overviews can be pages that halve in size. A mosaic file without GeoTIFF tags is placed at its mosaic tile ([\#3728](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3728>)).
- `martin cp --delete-meta KEY` deletes a metadata key, next to `--set-meta` ([\#1081](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/issues/1081>), [\#3777](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3777>)). `mbtiles meta-update` takes both flags ([\#3755](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3755>)).
- FreeBSD 14.0+ binaries for x86\_64 and aarch64, and an `x86_64-unknown-freebsd-legacycpu` tarball ([\#3783](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3783>)).
- `--features fips` builds Martin with FIPS 140-3 compliant TLS. No release binary is built with it. See [installation](<https://maplibre.org/martin/installation/>) ([\#3809](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3809>)).

### Fixed

- `--order-by` no longer breaks tables without an id column, which includes every auto-published table unless `id_columns` is set. Before, all their tiles failed with an SQL syntax error ([\#3762](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3762>)).
- Table `properties` keep the order the config lists them in. Before, they were sorted by name ([\#3810](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3810>)).
- A source no longer advertises zooms above 30 in its TileJSON. It is capped with a warning naming the source ([\#3772](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3772>)).
- A static image with a fractional pixel ratio, such as `@1.005x`, has its own size. Before, a cached `@1x` renderer answered it ([\#3753](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3753>)).
- Rendered image encodes stay limited to the number of cores when clients disconnect, for example while a map is panned quickly ([\#3750](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3750>)).
- A configuration error inside a `pmtiles`, `mbtiles`, `cog`, `geojson`, `styles`, `sprites` or `fonts` section points at the bad value instead of the section's first key ([\#3748](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3748>)).

### Unstable

> \[!WARNING\] None of this is in the release binaries. It needs a build with `--features unstable-generate`, and its configuration may still change.

- [`martin test`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-test/>) renders real rows through the `layers` of table sources in bulk mode, and keeps the result in a spec file ([\#3685](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3685>), [\#3686](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3686>), [\#3688](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3688>), [\#3696](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3696>), [\#3697](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3697>), [\#3741](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3741>), [\#3749](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3749>)). `generate` finds a row for each path a feature can take through a layer, and reviews new and changed cases in the terminal. `run` shows how the cases changed after a change to the layers.
- Bulk mode matches tile mode more closely: halves round to even ([\#3766](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3766>), [\#3778](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3778>)), what lies on a tile's buffer edge is kept ([\#3767](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3767>)), tiles for points and unclipped features are picked from the source geometry ([\#3780](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3780>)), simplification keeps the first of equally far vertices ([\#3779](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3779>)), unclipped features are whole in every tile any part reaches ([\#3731](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3731>)), MultiPolygon parts that round onto each other merge ([\#3752](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3752>)), a multipoint with an `EMPTY` part is kept ([\#3751](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3751>)), and MLT is encoded with the configured `convert_to_mlt` settings ([\#3761](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3761>)).
- A polygon ring in a tile that gets its whole polygon starts where `ST_AsMVTGeom` starts it. [`--mvt-quirk`](<https://maplibre.org/martin/martin-generate/#mvt-quirks>) `preserve-ring-start` keeps the source start, and `keep-unused-keys` lists every key the config gives a layer, as `ST_AsMVT` does ([\#3811](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3811>), [\#3812](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3812>)).
- Bulk mode stops on a geometry a tile cannot hold, such as a `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` or `TRIANGLE`, naming the source and feature and printing a query that counts such rows. Before, it skipped them or drew a wrong point ([\#3756](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3756>), [\#3757](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3757>)).
- Bulk mode reads `--mbtiles-type`, `--skip-agg-tiles-hash`, `--set-meta` and `--delete-meta`. The flags it cannot read each get their own reason, and a config with `max_feature_count` is refused instead of silently ignored ([\#3840](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3840>)).
- Bulk mode is faster on a Germany extract: CEL comparisons and boolean logic skip the interpreter (layered -9.6%) ([\#3830](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3830>)), up to 4096 sort runs merge at once instead of 256 (plain -4.8%) ([\#3831](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3831>)), and small polygons are checked without a grid (render CPU -8%) ([\#3832](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3832>)).
- DuckDB sources (`unstable-duckdb`) no longer publish a configured table a second time, nor take the id of a broken one, so `points.1` can become `points` ([\#3692](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3692>)).

### Other

- *(docs)* the OGC API and `martin test` with diagrams, five top-level tabs and a fuller troubleshooting page ([\#3773](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3773>), [\#3741](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3741>), [\#3743](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3743>))
- *(deps)* update `mlt-core` to 0.22.1, `spreet` to 0.14 (dropping the unmaintained `ttf-parser` and `rustybuzz`), `oxipng`, `similar`, `vt100`, `roxmltree`, the Docker images and the pre-commit hooks, and bump `ctutils` past RUSTSEC-2026-0385 ([\#3833](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3833>), [\#3781](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3781>), [\#3797](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3797>), [\#3790](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3790>), [\#3789](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3789>), [\#3788](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3788>), [\#3792](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3792>), [\#3791](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3791>), [\#3784](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3784>), [\#3785](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3785>), [\#3754](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3754>), [\#3740](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3740>), [\#3730](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3730>), [\#3798](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3798>), [\#3839](<https://github.com/maplibre/martin/pull/3839>))
